docs.title: Inspekt - Security Features
docs.text: This document explains the security model implemented in Inspekt extensions (both Chrome and Firefox).

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: To address concerns about arbitrary code execution and improve Chrome Web Store acceptance chances, we've implemented a comprehensive opt-in permission system.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. First Visit to Any Domain
  2. Content script loads but does NOT connect to WebSocket
  3. Permission check runs automatically

  4. If domain not allowed: Beautiful modal appears

  5. Permission Modal

  6. Clear heading: "Inspekt - Allow CLI control of this website?"
  7. Shows the domain name prominently
  8. Lists what Zen Bridge will be able to do
  9. Warning about only allowing trusted sites

  10. Two buttons: "Deny" or "Allow [domain]"

  11. After Permission Granted

  12. Domain saved to chrome.storage.sync (syncs across devices)
  13. WebSocket connection established
  14. Zen commands now work on this domain

  15. Permission persists across browser sessions

  16. Domain Management

  17. Extension popup shows all allowed domains
  18. Current domain status highlighted
  19. One-click to allow/remove domains
  20. Full transparency - see everywhere Zen has access

docs.title: User Experience Flow
docs.text:
User visits github.com
    ↓
Content script loads
    ↓
Checks: Is github.com allowed?
    ↓ NO
Shows permission modal
    ↓
User clicks "Allow github.com"
    ↓
Domain saved to storage
    ↓
WebSocket connects
    ↓
✓ Zen commands work

docs.title: Subsequent Visits
docs.text:
User visits github.com again
    ↓
Content script loads
    ↓
Checks: Is github.com allowed?
    ↓ YES (already in storage)
WebSocket connects immediately
    ↓
✓ Zen commands work (no modal)

docs.title: Storage
docs.text:
Location: chrome.storage.sync (or browser.storage.sync for Firefox)

Key: zen_allowed_domains

Value: Array of allowed domain strings

Example: 

{
  "zen_allowed_domains": [
    "github.com",
    "gmail.com",
    "localhost",
    "example.com"
  ]
}

Syncing: Permissions sync across all devices where user is signed in to Chrome/Firefox

docs.title: What We Store
docs.text:
• List of domains you've explicitly allowed
  • Stored locally using browser's storage API
  • Synced across your devices (via browser sync)

docs.title: What We DON'T Store
docs.text:
• No URLs or page content
  • No browsing history
  • No commands you run
  • No personal information
  • No analytics or tracking data

docs.title: Data Flow
docs.text:
Browser ←→ Extension ←→ localhost:8766 ←→ Your CLI

NO external servers
NO cloud services
NO data collection

docs.title: 1. Prevents Unauthorized Access
docs.text:
• Malicious websites can't automatically connect
  • You must explicitly allow each domain
  • No surprise connections

docs.title: 2. Least Privilege Principle
docs.text:
• Extension has permissions for <all_urls>
  • But ONLY activates on domains you allow
  • Unused permissions remain dormant

docs.title: 3. Transparent & Auditable
docs.text:
• See all allowed domains in popup
  • Revoke access anytime
  • Clear indication when Zen is active

docs.title: 4. User Control
docs.text:
• You decide which sites are safe
  • No blanket trust required
  • Fine-grained control per domain

docs.title: Files Involved
docs.text:
permissions.js (Content Script) - Handles domain permission checks - Shows opt-in modal - Manages storage operations - Loaded before main content script

content.js (Content Script) - Checks permission before connecting - Only establishes WebSocket if allowed - Respects user's permission decisions

popup.html/js/css (Extension Popup) - Displays current domain status - Lists all allowed domains - Allows adding/removing permissions - Visual management interface

manifest.json - Added storage permission - Loads permissions.js before content.js

docs.title: Key Functions
docs.text:
// Check if domain is allowed
ZenPermissions.isAllowed(domain)

// Show opt-in modal and wait for user decision
ZenPermissions.checkAndRequest()

// Add domain to allowed list
ZenPermissions.allowDomain(domain)

// Remove domain from allowed list
ZenPermissions.removeDomain(domain)

// Get all allowed domains
ZenPermissions.getAllowedDomains()

docs.title: Chrome Web Store Benefits
docs.text: This security model addresses Chrome Web Store's main concerns:

docs.title: 1. Arbitrary Code Execution
docs.text: Before: Extension could execute code on any website automatically Now: User must explicitly allow each domain first

docs.title: 2. Broad Permissions
docs.text: Before: <all_urls> looked dangerous without safeguards Now: Permission gated by user opt-in per domain

docs.title: 3. User Trust
docs.text: Before: Users couldn't control where extension worked Now: Full transparency and control

docs.title: 4. Security Disclosure
docs.text: Before: Hard to explain security model Now: Clear, visible permission system

docs.title: Permission Justification for Chrome Web Store
docs.text:
When submitting to Chrome Web Store, use this justification:

storage: 

Required to store user's domain permissions. Users must explicitly allow
each domain before the extension can control it. This list of allowed
domains is stored locally using chrome.storage.sync.

host_permissions (): 

Required to inject the content script that displays the permission modal
on all websites. The content script only establishes a connection AFTER
the user explicitly allows the domain. Users maintain full control over
which domains the extension can access.

docs.title: For End Users
docs.text:
Q: Do I need to allow every website? A: No! Only allow websites you actively want to control via Zen CLI. Most users only need 5-10 domains.

Q: What if I deny a domain by mistake? A: Open the extension popup, find the domain, and click "Allow This Domain". Or refresh the page to see the modal again.

Q: Can I revoke access later? A: Yes! Click the extension icon, find the domain in the list, and click "Remove".

Q: Do my permissions sync across computers? A: Yes, if you're signed in to Chrome/Firefox, your allowed domains sync automatically.

Q: Is this safe? A: Yes! You explicitly control which websites Zen can access. Plus, all communication stays between your browser and local CLI (localhost). No external servers involved.

docs.title: For Developers
docs.text:
Q: How do I test the permission modal? A: Clear storage (chrome.storage.sync.clear() in console) and refresh the page.

Q: Can I pre-allow domains programmatically? A: No, this would defeat the security model. Users must click "Allow" in the modal.

Q: Does this work offline? A: Yes, permissions are stored locally and don't require internet.

docs.title: Manual Testing
docs.text:
1. First Visit: 

    # Clear storage
chrome.storage.sync.clear()

# Visit new domain
# Modal should appear
# Click "Allow"
# WebSocket should connect

  2. Subsequent Visit: 

    # Visit same domain again
# No modal (already allowed)
# WebSocket connects automatically

  3. Popup Management: 

    # Open extension popup
# Should show current domain
# Should list all allowed domains
# Click "Remove" on a domain
# Refresh that domain's page
# Modal should appear again

docs.title: Automated Testing
docs.text: See tests/permissions_test.js (to be created) for automated permission tests.

docs.title: Future Enhancements
docs.text:
Possible improvements to consider:

  1. Temporary Permissions
  2. "Allow for this session only" option

  3. Permission expires when browser closes

  4. Subdomain Control

  5. Option to allow entire domain vs. specific subdomain

  6. Currently allows entire domain (e.g., *.github.com)

  7. Permission Groups

  8. Pre-defined groups (e.g., "Development Sites")

  9. Bulk allow/remove

  10. Activity Log

  11. Show which domains were accessed when

  12. Privacy-respecting local log

  13. Import/Export

  14. Export allowed domains to file
  15. Import on different browser/profile

docs.title: Comparison with Other Extensions
docs.text:
How Zen Bridge's security compares to similar tools:

Extension Permission Model Zen Bridge Tampermonkey Per-script URL patterns Per-domain opt-in Selenium IDE All URLs by default Explicit opt-in required Puppeteer Recorder All URLs by default Explicit opt-in required Chrome DevTools Built-in, always allowed User-controlled

Advantage: Zen Bridge gives users more control than most automation tools while maintaining full functionality.

docs.title: Compliance
docs.text:
This security model helps with:

  • ✅ Chrome Web Store policies
  • ✅ Firefox Add-ons policies
  • ✅ GDPR (no personal data collected)
  • ✅ User trust and transparency
  • ✅ Enterprise security requirements

  2. Verify domain is in allowed list
  3. Try removing and re-adding the domain
  4. Check browser console for errors
  5. Report issues: https://github.com/roelvangils/zen-bridge/issues

docs.title: Localhost-Only Communication

docs.title: How CSP Bypass Works
docs.text:
The extension uses Chrome's scripting.executeScript() API (Manifest V3) which has elevated privileges:

  1. Content script receives execution request from WebSocket
  2. Sends message to background service worker
  3. Background script uses scripting.executeScript() to bypass CSP
  4. Result is sent back via WebSocket

This is safe and intended - browser extensions can bypass CSP for legitimate purposes like developer tools, automation, and accessibility features.

📚 Quick Reference - Essential commands (inspect, inspected, click, type) - Page analysis commands (index, describe, ask) - Navigation commands (open, back, forward)

docs.title: Differences from Firefox Extension
docs.text:
The Chrome extension uses Manifest V3 while Firefox uses Manifest V2:

Feature Firefox (Manifest V2) Chrome (Manifest V3) Background Persistent background page Service worker (event-driven) API Namespace browser.* chrome.* Script Execution tabs.executeScript() scripting.executeScript() Permissions Combined in permissions Split into permissions and host_permissions

Both versions provide the same functionality and CSP bypass capabilities.

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Q: Why an extension instead of just a userscript? A: Userscripts are blocked by CSP on many important sites (GitHub, Gmail, banking). Extensions have elevated privileges and can bypass CSP.

Q: Is it safe to bypass CSP? A: Yes! Browser extensions are designed to have elevated privileges. CSP restrictions apply to web content, not to trusted browser extensions.

Q: Why Manifest V3? A: Chrome is phasing out Manifest V2 extensions. Manifest V3 is the future-proof standard for Chrome extensions.

Q: Will this work on Edge, Brave, or other Chromium browsers? A: Yes! This extension should work on any Chromium-based browser (Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, etc.). Just load it in developer mode.

Q: Can I use both userscript and extension? A: It's recommended to use only one at a time to avoid conflicts. The extension is the better choice for compatibility.

Q: When will it be on Chrome Web Store? A: We're preparing for submission! See CHROME_WEB_STORE.md for our publication roadmap and how you can help.

# Inspekt - Command Line Browser Automation

Control your browser from the terminal with AI-powered automation. Execute JavaScript, automate tasks, and interact with any website using natural language commands.

## 🚀 Key Features

🔒 **Secure & User-Controlled** - Explicit opt-in required for each domain. You choose which websites Zen can access.

✨ **Works on ALL Websites** - Uses proper extension APIs to work on GitHub, Gmail, banking sites, and more (with your permission)

🤖 **AI-Powered Automation** - Use natural language commands like "click login button" or "fill out the form"

⚡ **DevTools Integration** - Store inspected elements with `inspektStore($0)` and manipulate them from CLI

🔒 **100% Local** - All communication stays between your browser and local CLI. No cloud, no tracking, complete privacy.

🛠️ **Developer-Friendly** - Perfect for web scraping, testing, automation, and rapid prototyping

## 🔐 Security First

**You're in control:** Zen Bridge requires your explicit permission before accessing any website.

1. Visit a new website → Permission modal appears
2. Review what access means → Allow or deny
3. Permission saved → Manage anytime from extension popup
4. Full transparency → See all allowed domains

Only websites YOU explicitly allow can be controlled from the CLI. Revoke access anytime.

4. **Run Commands**:
   ```bash
   inspekteval "document.title"
   inspektdo "click login button"
   inspektdescribe
   ```

- **Testing**: Test web applications from the command line
- **Data Extraction**: Extract data from websites programmatically
- **Debugging**: Execute JavaScript directly from your terminal
- **Prototyping**: Quickly test ideas without writing full scripts

- ✅ **Your Data Stays Yours** - All processing happens locally

inspektinfo

# Extract all links
inspektlinks

# Natural language interaction

### Privacy Practices

This extension enables command-line control of Chrome for browser automation, testing, and web interaction by establishing a local WebSocket connection between the browser and a CLI tool.

Required to inject and execute code with proper CSP bypass capabilities, enabling the extension to work on all websites including those with strict Content Security Policies. Users must explicitly allow each domain before the extension can access it.

Required to store user's domain permissions. The extension requires users to explicitly allow each domain before it can be controlled from the CLI. This list of allowed domains is stored locally using chrome.storage.sync.

Required to inject the content script that displays the permission modal on all websites. The content script only establishes a connection AFTER the user explicitly allows the domain. Users maintain full control over which domains the extension can access.

## Data Collection

Inspekt does NOT collect, store, or transmit any user data. The extension operates entirely locally on your machine.

docs.title: Testing Extension Changes
docs.text: After making changes to any extension files, follow these steps to test:

docs.title: 1. Reload the Extension
docs.text:
1. Navigate to chrome://extensions/
  2. Locate the "Inspekt" extension
  3. Click the Reload button (circular arrow icon)
  4. Verify no errors appear in the extension card

docs.title: 2. Refresh the Webpage
docs.text:
1. Go to the tab with your test webpage
  2. Perform a hard refresh:
  3. Mac: Cmd + Shift + R
  4. Windows/Linux: Ctrl + Shift + F5
  5. This clears cached scripts and ensures fresh content loads

docs.title: 3. Restart DevTools
docs.text:
1. Close DevTools completely (Cmd + Option + I or click X)
  2. Reopen DevTools (F12 or Cmd + Option + I)
  3. Navigate to the Inspekt panel

docs.title: 4. Verify Connection Status
docs.text:
1. Check the connection indicator in the Inspekt panel header
  2. Should show "Connected" (green dot) when server is running
  3. If showing "Checking…" or "Disconnected", check:
  4. Server is running (inspekt server start)
  5. No JavaScript errors in DevTools console
  6. Check page console for WebSocket connection logs

docs.title: Opening DevTools for the DevTools Panel
docs.text:
To debug the Inspekt panel itself:

  1. Open DevTools (F12)
  2. Right-click anywhere in the DevTools interface
  3. Select "Inspect" from context menu
  4. A new DevTools window opens - this is "DevTools for DevTools"
  5. Check Console tab for JavaScript errors in the panel code

docs.title: "Checking…" Status Persists
docs.text:
Cause: Extension not reloaded or cached version still active

Fix: 1. Reload extension in chrome://extensions/ 2. Hard refresh webpage (Cmd + Shift + R) 3. Close and reopen DevTools 4. Check DevTools console for errors

docs.title: JavaScript Syntax Errors
docs.text:
Cause: Template literal syntax errors (escaped backticks/dollar signs)

Fix: 1. Run ESLint: cd extensions/chrome && npm run lint 2. Fix reported errors 3. Follow reload procedure above

docs.title: WebSocket Connection Failed
docs.text:
Cause: Server not running or wrong port

Fix: 1. Start server: inspekt server start 2. Check server logs in terminal 3. Verify WebSocket connection in page console

docs.title: Checking Connection Status Variable
docs.text:
In the page console (not DevTools console):

// Check connection status
window.__INSPEKT_WS_CONNECTED__
// Should return: true (connected), 'connecting', or false (disconnected)

docs.title: Chrome Extension Contexts
docs.text: The extension operates in multiple JavaScript contexts:

docs.title: 1. Service Worker (background.js)
docs.text:
• Purpose: Handle extension logic, privileged APIs
  • APIs: Full chrome.* API access
  • No Access: DOM, page variables

docs.title: 2. Content Script (content.js)
docs.text:
• Purpose: Bridge between page and extension
  • APIs: Limited chrome.* APIs, DOM access
  • No Access: Page JavaScript variables

docs.title: 3. DevTools Panel (panel.html/panel.js)
docs.text:
• Purpose: UI and interaction
  • APIs: chrome.devtools.* APIs
  • Access: Can eval code in page context

docs.title: 4. Page Context (via injection)
docs.text:
• Purpose: Execute in page's JavaScript environment
  • APIs: Page variables, DOM
  • No Access: Extension APIs

docs.title: Module Not Loading
docs.text:
Symptom: Module fails to import, console shows module errors

Check: 1. File path is correct (case-sensitive) 2. File has .js extension in import 3. Module uses export keyword 4. No syntax errors in the file

docs.title: Event Handlers Not Working
docs.text:
Symptom: Clicks, keyboard shortcuts don't respond

Check: 1. Event listener registered after DOM ready 2. Element ID matches between HTML and JavaScript 3. No errors in console preventing script execution 4. Event propagation not stopped by another handler

docs.title: Connection Status Not Updating
docs.text:
Symptom: Shows "Checking…" despite WebSocket connected

Check: 1. Extension reloaded in chrome://extensions/ 2. DevTools reopened after reload 3. window.__INSPEKT_WS_CONNECTED__ is true in page console 4. connection-manager.js logging shows status checks 5. No JavaScript errors in DevTools console

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always reload extension after JavaScript changes
  2. Hard refresh page after extension reload
  3. Reopen DevTools after page refresh
  4. Check both consoles: Page console AND DevTools console
  5. Use logging: Add console.log() for debugging
  6. Run ESLint before committing changes
  7. Test in multiple tabs to verify WebSocket handling

docs.title: Manager Pattern
docs.text:
Used for core services that manage state and UI synchronization: - ConnectionManager - WebSocket status - SettingsManager - Settings persistence - ThemeManager - Theme state - HistoryManager - Element history tracking

export class Manager {
    constructor() {
        // DOM references
        // State
    }

    init() {
        this.load();
        this.setupEventListeners();
    }

    setupEventListeners() { }
    load() { }
    save() { }
}

docs.title: Component Pattern
docs.text:
Used for UI components with encapsulated behavior: - QuickActions - Action buttons - ElementPicker - Element picker activation - ElementHighlighter - Spotlight effects

export class Component {
    constructor(dependencies) {
        // Inject dependencies
    }

    render() { }
    handleEvent() { }
}

docs.title: Utility Pattern
docs.text:
Used for stateless helper functions: - clipboard.js - Copy operations - time.js - Time formatting - devtools.js - API wrappers

export function utilityFunction(params) {
    // Pure function
    return result;
}

docs.title: Inspekt - Firefox Extension
docs.text:
⚠️ Note: The Firefox extension is currently not actively maintained. The Chrome extension has more features including VM support, replay mode, and screencast integration. We recommend using Chrome/Chromium for the best Inspekt experience. Firefox support may be revisited in a future release.

The Firefox extension for Inspekt that bypasses CSP restrictions and works on all websites including GitHub, Gmail, banking sites, and more.

docs.title: Features
docs.text: ✨ CSP Bypass - Works on all websites, no restrictions 🔒 Explicit Opt-In - You control which domains Zen can access 🚀 Automatic Connection - Connects to localhost:8766 automatically 🛠️ DevTools Integration - Use inspektStore($0) in console 📊 Status Panel - Built-in settings panel with connection status and domain management 🔄 Auto-Reconnect - Maintains connection across page reloads ⚡ Manifest V2 - Uses latest Chrome extension architecture

docs.title: Method 3: Chrome Web Store (Coming Soon)
docs.text: Once published to the Chrome Web Store, you'll be able to install with one click. See CHROME_WEB_STORE.md for our publication roadmap.

docs.title: 1. Start the Zen Server
docs.text: inspektserver start

docs.title: 2. Open Any Website and Allow It
docs.text:
When you first visit a website, you'll see a permission modal:

  1. Navigate to a website (e.g., github.com, gmail.com)
  2. Permission modal appears - "Allow CLI control of this website?"
  3. Click "Allow [domain]" to grant permission for that entire domain
  4. Connection established - Inspekt is now active on that site

The extension remembers your choice, so you only need to allow each domain once. You can manage allowed domains from the extension popup.

Security: You must explicitly allow each domain before Inspekt can control it. This prevents unauthorized access and gives you full control.

docs.title: 3. Run Zen Commands
docs.text:
# Get page info
inspektinfo

# Extract title
inspekteval "document.title"

# Natural language actions
inspektdo "click login button"

# AI-powered description
inspektdescribe

# And any other inspektcommand!

docs.title: 4. Manage Domains via Status Panel
docs.text: Click the ⚡ icon in your toolbar to: - View connection status (green = connected, yellow = connecting, red = disconnected) - See current domain status - Allowed or not allowed - Allow/remove current domain - One-click permission management - View all allowed domains - See everywhere Inspekt has access - Remove domains - Revoke access anytime - Quick start guide and common commands

docs.title: Advantages Over Userscript
docs.text:
Feature Userscript Extension Works on GitHub ❌ Blocked by CSP ✅ Yes Works on Gmail ❌ Blocked by CSP ✅ Yes Works on Banking Sites ❌ Blocked by CSP ✅ Yes Installation Easier (one click) Slightly more steps Auto-Update Via Tampermonkey Via Chrome Web Store (when published) Settings Panel ❌ No ✅ Yes Status Indicator ❌ No ✅ Yes

Recommendation: Use the extension for full compatibility on all websites!

docs.title: Explicit Opt-In Per Domain
docs.text:
You're in control. Inspekt requires explicit permission before it can access any website:

  1. First Visit - Permission modal appears
  2. You Decide - Allow or deny access for that domain
  3. Saved Choice - Extension remembers your decision
  4. Manage Anytime - View and revoke permissions from the popup

Why this matters: - Prevents unauthorized access to your sensitive sites - You choose exactly which domains Zen can control - Permissions persist across sessions but can be revoked anytime - Transparent - see all allowed domains in the settings panel

docs.title: Localhost-Only Communication
docs.text:
All communication stays between: - Your browser (extension) - Your local CLI (localhost:8766)

No external servers. No tracking. No data collection.

docs.title: How CSP Bypass Works
docs.text:
The extension uses Chrome's tabs.executeScript() API (Manifest V2) which has elevated privileges:

  1. Content script receives execution request from WebSocket
  2. Sends message to background background script
  3. Background script uses tabs.executeScript() to bypass CSP
  4. Result is sent back via WebSocket

This is safe and intended - browser extensions can bypass CSP for legitimate purposes like developer tools, automation, and accessibility features.

The Chrome extension uses Manifest V2 while Firefox uses Manifest V2:

docs.title: FAQ
docs.text:
Q: Why an extension instead of just a userscript? A: Userscripts are blocked by CSP on many important sites (GitHub, Gmail, banking). Extensions have elevated privileges and can bypass CSP.

Q: Is it safe to bypass CSP? A: Yes! Browser extensions are designed to have elevated privileges. CSP restrictions apply to web content, not to trusted browser extensions.

Q: Why Manifest V2? A: Chrome is phasing out Manifest V2 extensions. Manifest V2 is the future-proof standard for Chrome extensions.

Q: Will this work on Edge, Brave, or other Chromium browsers? A: Yes! This extension should work on any Chromium-based browser (Edge, Brave, Opera, Vivaldi, etc.). Just load it in developer mode.

Q: Can I use both userscript and extension? A: It's recommended to use only one at a time to avoid conflicts. The extension is the better choice for compatibility.

Q: When will it be on Chrome Web Store? A: We're preparing for submission! See CHROME_WEB_STORE.md for our publication roadmap and how you can help.

docs.title: Permanent Installation Guide
docs.text: This guide explains how to install the Inspekt extension permanently in Firefox.

docs.title: Quick Answer
docs.text:
For regular Firefox users: The easiest way is to reload the temporary extension each time you restart Firefox (Method 1 below). We're working on submitting to the Firefox Add-ons store for one-click permanent installation.

For developers: Use Firefox Developer Edition with unsigned extensions enabled (Method 2 below).

docs.title: Method 1: Temporary Installation (Easiest)
docs.text:
Pros: - No special setup required - Works with regular Firefox - Perfect for testing and development

Cons: - Needs to be reloaded after Firefox restarts

docs.title: Steps:
docs.text:
1. Navigate to about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox
  2. Click "Load Temporary Add-on…"
  3. Select manifest.json from the extensions/firefox/ directory

Note: You'll need to repeat these steps each time you restart Firefox.

docs.title: Method 2: Self-Hosted Unsigned Extension (Developer Edition/Nightly)
docs.text:
Pros: - Permanent installation - No signing required - Full control

Cons: - Requires Firefox Developer Edition or Nightly - Need to disable signature verification

docs.title: 2.1 Install Firefox Developer Edition or Nightly
docs.text: Download one of these: - Firefox Developer Edition: https://www.mozilla.org/firefox/developer/ - Firefox Nightly: https://www.mozilla.org/firefox/nightly/

docs.title: 2.2 Build the Extension
docs.text:
cd extensions/firefox
./build.sh

This creates build/zen-browser-bridge-4.0.0.xpi

docs.title: 2.3 Disable Signature Verification
docs.text:
1. Open Firefox Developer Edition/Nightly
  2. Navigate to about:config
  3. Accept the risk warning
  4. Search for xpinstall.signatures.required
  5. Set it to false (double-click to toggle)

docs.title: 2.4 Install the Extension
docs.text:
Option A: Drag and Drop 1. Open Firefox 2. Drag build/zen-browser-bridge-4.0.0.xpi into Firefox window 3. Click "Add" when prompted

Option B: File Picker 1. Navigate to about:addons 2. Click the gear icon (⚙️) 3. Select "Install Add-on From File…" 4. Choose build/zen-browser-bridge-4.0.0.xpi 5. Click "Add" when prompted

The extension is now permanently installed!

docs.title: Method 3: Web Extension Signing (Recommended for Distribution)
docs.text:
Pros: - Works with regular Firefox - Permanent installation - Can be shared with others - Most secure method

Cons: - Requires Mozilla Developer account - Takes time for review (if distributing publicly)

docs.title: 3.1 Get a Mozilla Add-on Developer Account
docs.text:
1. Go to https://addons.mozilla.org/developers/
  2. Sign in with Firefox Account (or create one)
  3. Agree to the Developer Agreement

docs.title: 3.2 Build the Extension
docs.text:
cd extensions/firefox
./build.sh

This creates build/zen-browser-bridge-4.0.0.zip

docs.title: 3.3 Option A: Self-Distribution (Unlisted)
docs.text:
Use this if you want to host the extension yourself (not on the store):

  1. Go to https://addons.mozilla.org/developers/addon/submit/upload-unlisted
  2. Upload build/zen-browser-bridge-4.0.0.zip
  3. Wait for automated validation (usually instant)
  4. Download the signed .xpi file
  5. Distribute the signed .xpi to users

Advantages: - No review process - Fast (usually minutes) - Can distribute via your own website/GitHub

How users install: - Users download the signed .xpi - Drag and drop into Firefox - Extension stays permanently installed

docs.title: 3.4 Option B: Firefox Add-ons Store (Listed)
docs.text:
Use this for public distribution on the official store:

  1. Go to https://addons.mozilla.org/developers/addon/submit/distribution
  2. Choose "On this site" (listed)
  3. Upload build/zen-browser-bridge-4.0.0.zip
  4. Fill out listing information:
  5. Name: Inspekt
  6. Summary: Execute JavaScript in your browser from the command line
  7. Categories: Developer Tools
  8. Support email/website
  9. Submit for review

Review process: - Mozilla reviews the extension (can take days to weeks) - Once approved, it appears on addons.mozilla.org - Users can install with one click

Advantages: - Maximum visibility and trust - One-click installation for users - Automatic updates

docs.title: Method 4: Use web-ext for Development
docs.text: Best for: Active development and testing

docs.title: 4.1 Install web-ext
docs.text:
npm install -g web-ext

Or use npx (no installation needed): 

npx web-ext --version

docs.title: 4.2 Run Extension in Temporary Profile
docs.text:
cd extensions/firefox
web-ext run

This opens a new Firefox window with the extension loaded.

docs.title: 4.3 Run with Your Firefox Profile
docs.text: web-ext run --firefox-profile=/path/to/profile

docs.title: 4.4 Build and Sign
docs.text:
# Build
web-ext build

# Sign (requires API credentials)
web-ext sign --api-key=your-key --api-secret=your-secret

Get API credentials: 1. Go to https://addons.mozilla.org/developers/addon/api/key/ 2. Generate API credentials 3. Use them with web-ext

docs.title: Comparison Table
docs.text: Method Permanent Regular Firefox Setup Complexity Best For Temporary ❌ No ✅ Yes ⭐ Easy Testing, quick use Unsigned (Dev Edition) ✅ Yes ❌ No ⭐⭐ Medium Development Self-Signed (Unlisted) ✅ Yes ✅ Yes ⭐⭐⭐ Medium Self-distribution Store (Listed) ✅ Yes ✅ Yes ⭐⭐⭐⭐ Hard Public distribution web-ext ❌ Temporary ✅ Yes ⭐⭐ Medium Active development

docs.title: For Personal Use
docs.text: → Method 2 (Unsigned) with Firefox Developer Edition - One-time setup, permanent installation - No review process

docs.title: For Sharing with Friends/Team
docs.text: → Method 3A (Self-Signed Unlisted) - Fast signing (minutes) - Share the signed .xpi file - Works on regular Firefox

docs.title: For Public Release
docs.text: → Method 3B (Store Listed) - Maximum trust and visibility - Users can find it by searching - Automatic updates

docs.title: "This add-on could not be installed because it appears to be corrupt"
docs.text: Solution: Make sure you're using Firefox Developer Edition/Nightly with signature verification disabled, or use a signed .xpi file.

docs.title: "Install Add-on From File" is greyed out
docs.text: Solution: This feature requires Firefox Developer Edition, Beta, Nightly, or ESR. It's disabled in regular Firefox for security.

docs.title: Extension disappears after Firefox restart (Temporary Installation)
docs.text: Solution: This is expected behavior. Use Method 2 or 3 for permanent installation.

docs.title: Signature verification setting doesn't persist
docs.text: Solution: - This is only supported in Developer Edition and Nightly - Regular Firefox doesn't allow disabling signature verification - Use signed extensions instead

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
Once you have the extension permanently installed:

  1. Start the server: 

    inspektserver start

  2. Test on a CSP-protected site: 

    # Open github.com in your browser, then:
inspektinfo
inspekteval "document.title"

  3. Enjoy CSP bypass on all websites! ⚡

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text: Customize Inspekt for your specific workflow with comprehensive configuration options. This guide covers everything from basic settings to advanced control mode customization.

docs.title: Configuration File Location
docs.text:
Inspekt uses a JSON configuration file:

config.json

The file is located in the project root directory where you installed Inspekt.

Create Config File

If config.json doesn't exist, create it in the project root: 

cd /path/to/inspekt-bridge
touch config.json

docs.title: Configuration Structure
docs.text:
The configuration file has two main sections:

  1. ai-language - Language for AI operations (summarize, describe)
  2. control - Keyboard control mode settings

docs.title: Complete Default Configuration
docs.text:
{
  "ai-language": "auto",
  "control": {
    "auto-refocus": "only-spa",
    "focus-outline": "custom",
    "speak-name": false,
    "speak-all": true,
    "announce-role": false,
    "announce-on-page-load": false,
    "navigation-wrap": true,
    "scroll-on-focus": true,
    "click-delay": 0,
    "focus-color": "#0066ff",
    "focus-size": 3,
    "focus-animation": true,
    "focus-glow": true,
    "sound-on-focus": "none",
    "selector-strategy": "id-first",
    "refocus-timeout": 2000,
    "verbose": true,
    "verbose-logging": false
  }
}

docs.title: ai-language
docs.text:
Controls the language used for AI-powered features (inspektsummarize and inspektdescribe).

Type: string Default: "auto" Options: "auto", "en", "nl", "fr", "de", "es", etc.

Auto-detect (Default)Fixed LanguageMultiple Languages 
{
  "ai-language": "auto"
}

Automatically detects the page language and uses it for AI operations.

{
  "ai-language": "en"
}

Always use English for AI operations, regardless of page language.

{
  "ai-language": "nl"
}

Use Dutch for summaries and descriptions.

Supported Languages: Any language code supported by your AI provider (mods).

Requires mods

AI features require mods to be installed. The language setting is passed to the AI model in the prompt.

docs.title: Control Mode Configuration
docs.text: The control section customizes keyboard navigation behavior when using inspektcontrol.

docs.title: auto-refocus
docs.text:
When to automatically refocus the previously focused element after page navigation.

Type: "always" | "only-spa" | "never" Default: "only-spa"

only-spa (Default)alwaysnever 
{
  "control": {
    "auto-refocus": "only-spa"
  }
}

Only refocus on Single Page Applications (SPAs) where the URL changes without a full page reload.

Use case: Modern web apps like Gmail, Twitter, GitHub.

{
  "control": {
    "auto-refocus": "always"
  }
}

Always try to refocus after any page change, including full page reloads.

Use case: Aggressive refocus behavior for maximum continuity.

{
  "control": {
    "auto-refocus": "never"
  }
}

Never automatically refocus. Focus returns to <body> after navigation.

Use case: You prefer manual navigation from the top of each page.

docs.title: refocus-timeout
docs.text:
Maximum time to wait for refocus operation to complete.

Type: number (milliseconds) Default: 2000 Range: 100 - 10000

{
  "control": {
    "refocus-timeout": 2000
  }
}

Increase for slow-loading pages, decrease for faster feedback.

docs.title: focus-outline
docs.text:
Visual style for focused elements.

Type: "custom" | "original" | "none" Default: "custom"

custom (Default)originalnone 
{
  "control": {
    "focus-outline": "custom"
  }
}

Use Inspekt's custom blue outline with glow effect.

{
  "control": {
    "focus-outline": "original"
  }
}

Keep the browser's default focus outline.

{
  "control": {
    "focus-outline": "none"
  }
}

No focus outline (not recommended for accessibility).

docs.title: focus-color
docs.text:
Color of the custom focus outline.

Type: string (CSS color) Default: "#0066ff"

{
  "control": {
    "focus-color": "#ff6600"
  }
}

Examples:

  • "#0066ff" - Blue (default)
  • "#ff0000" - Red
  • "rgb(255, 0, 0)" - Red (RGB)
  • "orange" - Orange (named color)

docs.title: focus-size
docs.text:
Width of the focus outline in pixels.

Type: number (pixels) Default: 3 Range: 1 - 10

{
  "control": {
    "focus-size": 5
  }
}

Larger values create more prominent outlines.

docs.title: focus-animation
docs.text:
Enable animated focus transitions.

Type: boolean Default: true

{
  "control": {
    "focus-animation": true
  }
}

Smooth fade-in effect when focus changes.

docs.title: focus-glow
docs.text:
Enable glow effect around focused elements.

Type: boolean Default: true

{
  "control": {
    "focus-glow": true
  }
}

Adds a soft glow shadow for better visibility.

docs.title: navigation-wrap
docs.text:
Whether navigation wraps from last element to first (and vice versa).

Type: boolean Default: true

{
  "control": {
    "navigation-wrap": true
  }
}

When true, pressing Tab on the last focusable element jumps to the first.

docs.title: scroll-on-focus
docs.text:
Automatically scroll focused elements into view.

Type: boolean Default: true

{
  "control": {
    "scroll-on-focus": true
  }
}

Ensures focused elements are always visible.

docs.title: click-delay
docs.text:
Delay before executing click actions (in milliseconds).

Type: number (milliseconds) Default: 0 Range: 0 - 5000

{
  "control": {
    "click-delay": 100
  }
}

Useful if pages need time to settle before clicks.

docs.title: sound-on-focus
docs.text:
Play a sound when focus changes.

Type: "none" | "beep" | "click" | "subtle" Default: "none"

none (Default)beepclicksubtle 
{
  "control": {
    "sound-on-focus": "none"
  }
}

No sound effects.

{
  "control": {
    "sound-on-focus": "beep"
  }
}

Short beep on focus change.

{
  "control": {
    "sound-on-focus": "click"
  }
}

Click sound on focus change.

{
  "control": {
    "sound-on-focus": "subtle"
  }
}

Subtle tone on focus change.

Browser Support

Sound effects require browser support for the Web Audio API.

docs.title: speak-all
docs.text:
Speak all terminal output via text-to-speech (macOS only).

Type: boolean Default: true

{
  "control": {
    "speak-all": true
  }
}

Uses macOS say command to read terminal messages aloud.

docs.title: speak-name
docs.text:
Speak element name when focused.

Type: boolean Default: false

{
  "control": {
    "speak-name": true
  }
}

Announces accessible name of focused element (from aria-label, text content, etc.).

docs.title: announce-role
docs.text:
Announce element role (button, link, heading, etc.).

Type: boolean Default: false

{
  "control": {
    "announce-role": true
  }
}

Example: "Submit button" instead of just "Submit".

docs.title: announce-on-page-load
docs.text:
Announce page title when a new page loads.

Type: boolean Default: false

{
  "control": {
    "announce-on-page-load": true
  }
}

Helps orient you when navigating between pages.

docs.title: selector-strategy
docs.text:
Strategy for generating element selectors for refocus operations.

Type: "id-first" | "aria-first" | "css-first" Default: "id-first"

id-first (Default)aria-firstcss-first 
{
  "control": {
    "selector-strategy": "id-first"
  }
}

Prefer id attributes, fall back to ARIA, then CSS selectors.

Best for: Most web pages with proper IDs.

{
  "control": {
    "selector-strategy": "aria-first"
  }
}

Prefer ARIA labels, fall back to ID, then CSS.

Best for: Accessibility-focused applications.

{
  "control": {
    "selector-strategy": "css-first"
  }
}

Use CSS selectors based on tag/class/structure.

Best for: Pages with dynamic IDs.

docs.title: verbose
docs.text:
Show detailed terminal announcements during control mode.

Type: boolean Default: true

{
  "control": {
    "verbose": true
  }
}

When true, prints messages like "Focused: Submit button" to the terminal.

docs.title: verbose-logging
docs.text:
Enable verbose logging in the browser console.

Type: boolean Default: false

{
  "control": {
    "verbose-logging": true
  }
}

Useful for debugging control mode behavior. Check browser DevTools console.

docs.title: Minimal Configuration
docs.text:
For users who just want AI in a different language:

{
  "ai-language": "nl"
}

All control settings use defaults.

docs.title: Accessibility-Focused Configuration
docs.text:
For users relying on screen readers and audio feedback:

{
  "ai-language": "en",
  "control": {
    "auto-refocus": "always",
    "speak-all": true,
    "speak-name": true,
    "announce-role": true,
    "announce-on-page-load": true,
    "sound-on-focus": "subtle",
    "verbose": true,
    "selector-strategy": "aria-first"
  }
}

docs.title: Performance-Optimized Configuration
docs.text:
Minimal visual effects for faster performance:

{
  "ai-language": "auto",
  "control": {
    "focus-animation": false,
    "focus-glow": false,
    "scroll-on-focus": false,
    "speak-all": false,
    "verbose": false,
    "verbose-logging": false
  }
}

docs.title: High-Contrast Configuration
docs.text:
Enhanced visibility with bold outlines:

{
  "ai-language": "auto",
  "control": {
    "focus-outline": "custom",
    "focus-color": "#ffff00",
    "focus-size": 5,
    "focus-animation": true,
    "focus-glow": true
  }
}

docs.title: Developer/Debug Configuration
docs.text:
Maximum logging and visibility:

{
  "ai-language": "auto",
  "control": {
    "auto-refocus": "always",
    "verbose": true,
    "verbose-logging": true,
    "refocus-timeout": 5000,
    "focus-color": "#ff00ff",
    "focus-size": 4
  }
}

docs.title: Reload Configuration
docs.text:
Configuration is loaded when:

  1. Server starts - inspektserver start
  2. Control mode starts - inspektcontrol

To apply changes:

Restart Control ModeRestart Server 
# Press 'q' in control mode to quit, then restart
inspektcontrol

inspektserver stop
inspektserver start --daemon

Live Reload

Control mode configuration is sent to the browser when you start inspektcontrol, so you just need to quit and restart control mode to apply changes.

docs.title: Customizing AI Prompts
docs.text: AI prompts are stored in separate files for easy customization:

docs.title: Summary Prompt
docs.text:
Location: prompts/summary.prompt

Edit this file to change how articles are summarized:

Provide a concise, structured summary of the following article.
Focus on the main points and key takeaways.

Article content:
{content}

docs.title: Description Prompt
docs.text:
Location: prompts/describe.prompt

Edit this file to change how pages are described:

Describe this webpage in a way that would be helpful for someone
using a screen reader. Focus on navigation, main content, and structure.

Page structure:
{content}

Variables available: {content}, {url}, {title}, {language}

docs.title: Configuration Hierarchy
docs.text:
Configuration is loaded in the following order (later values override earlier ones):

  1. Default values (hardcoded in inspekt/domain/models.py)
  2. config.json (project root)
  3. Command-line flags (where applicable)

Example:

# Default verbose=true, but config.json sets verbose=false
# Result: verbose=false

# But if you pass a flag:
inspektcontrol --verbose
# Result: verbose=true (flag overrides config)

No CLI Flags for Config

Currently, Inspekt doesn't support command-line flags for most configuration options. Edit config.json to customize behavior.

docs.title: Configuration Not Loading
docs.text:
Problem: Changes to config.json don't seem to apply.

Solutions:

  1. Check JSON syntax: 

    # Validate JSON
python3 -c "import json; json.load(open('config.json'))"

  2. Check file location: 

    # Ensure config.json is in project root
ls -la config.json

  3. Restart server and control mode: 

    inspektserver stop
inspektserver start --daemon
inspektcontrol

docs.title: Invalid Configuration Value
docs.text:
Problem: Server or control mode fails to start.

Solution: Check for invalid values:

  • auto-refocus: Must be "always", "only-spa", or "never"
  • focus-outline: Must be "custom", "original", or "none"
  • sound-on-focus: Must be "none", "beep", "click", or "subtle"
  • selector-strategy: Must be "id-first", "aria-first", or "css-first"
  • refocus-timeout: Must be number >= 100
  • focus-size: Must be number >= 1

docs.title: Configuration Ignored
docs.text:
Problem: Some settings don't seem to work.

Check:

  1. Feature support: Some features (like TTS) only work on macOS
  2. Browser compatibility: Sound effects require Web Audio API
  3. Spelling: JSON keys are case-sensitive and use hyphens

docs.title: Advanced: Programmatic Configuration
docs.text:
You can load and validate configuration programmatically:

from inspekt.domain.models import InspektConfig

# Load from file
with open('config.json') as f:
    config_dict = json.load(f)

# Validate with Pydantic
config = InspektConfig(**config_dict)

# Access settings
print(config.ai_language)  # "auto"
print(config.control.auto_refocus)  # "only-spa"
print(config.control.focus_color)  # "#0066ff"

This is useful for building extensions or integrating Inspekt into other tools.

docs.title: Recording and Replay Audio
docs.text: The audio section controls audio feedback during inspekt record and inspekt replay.

docs.title: audio.output
docs.text:
Where to play audio feedback sounds.

Type: "cli" | "browser" | "off" Default: "cli"

cli (Default)browseroff 
{
  "audio": {
    "output": "cli"
  }
}

Play sounds via system audio (macOS afplay, Linux aplay).

Advantages: - Works immediately, no browser interaction needed - Plays asynchronously, doesn't slow down replay - Works over SSH if your terminal supports audio

{
  "audio": {
    "output": "browser"
  }
}

Play sounds via Web Audio API in the browser.

Note: Requires clicking in the browser window first (browser autoplay policy).

Use case: When terminal audio is not available.

{
  "audio": {
    "output": "off"
  }
}

Disable all audio feedback.

Use case: CI/CD environments, quiet operation.

docs.title: audio.volume
docs.text:
Volume level for audio feedback.

Type: number (0.0 to 1.0) Default: 0.5

{
  "audio": {
    "output": "cli",
    "volume": 0.7
  }
}

docs.title: Replay Configuration
docs.text: The replay section controls behavior of inspekt replay.

docs.title: replay.validate
docs.text:
Whether to run preflight validation before replaying recordings.

Type: boolean Default: true

Validation checks for: - YAML syntax errors - Missing external files (for uploads) - Invalid action types - Timestamp anomalies - Large time gaps between steps

Enabled (Default)Disabled 
{
  "replay": {
    "validate": true
  }
}

Validates recordings before replay. Shows errors that block replay and warnings that prompt for confirmation.

{
  "replay": {
    "validate": false
  }
}

Skips validation for faster replay startup. Use when you trust the recording files or in CI environments where recordings have been pre-validated.

Per-command override

You can skip validation for a single replay without changing config: 

inspekt replay my-recording.yaml --skip-validation

See inspekt validate for standalone validation.

docs.title: Record Configuration
docs.text: The record section controls behavior of inspekt record.

docs.title: record.max-actions-per-second
docs.text:
Rate limit to prevent runaway recordings from held keys or infinite loops.

Type: number Default: 10 Range: 1 - 100

{
  "record": {
    "max-actions-per-second": 10
  }
}

When exceeded, recording automatically stops and saves with a warning.

docs.title: record.synthetic-dialogs
docs.text:
Use non-blocking HTML overlays instead of native alert(), confirm(), and prompt() dialogs during recording.

Type: boolean Default: false

Native Dialogs (Default)Synthetic Dialogs 
{
  "record": {
    "synthetic-dialogs": false
  }
}

Native browser dialogs appear when the page calls alert(), confirm(), or prompt(). These block JavaScript execution until you interact with them.

Use case: Manual testing where you want authentic user experience.

{
  "record": {
    "synthetic-dialogs": true
  }
}

Styled HTML overlays appear instead of native dialogs. These don't block JavaScript - functions return immediately with default values.

Use cases: - AI agent recording - Browser automation - CI/CD environments - Headless browser testing

CLI Override

Enable for a single recording without changing config: 

inspekt record --synthetic-dialogs my-recording.yaml

See JavaScript Dialogs in Recording for detailed usage.

docs.title: Configuration Reference
docs.text:
Quick reference for all available settings:

Setting Type Default Description ai-language string "auto" Language for AI operations audio.output string "cli" Audio output: cli, browser, or off audio.volume number 0.5 Audio volume (0.0 to 1.0) record.max-actions-per-second number 10 Rate limit for recording (actions/sec) record.synthetic-dialogs boolean false Use non-blocking HTML overlays for JS dialogs replay.validate boolean true Run preflight validation before replay control.auto-refocus string "only-spa" When to auto-refocus control.focus-outline string "custom" Focus outline style control.speak-name boolean false Speak element name control.speak-all boolean true Speak all terminal output control.announce-role boolean false Announce element role control.announce-on-page-load boolean false Announce page title on load control.navigation-wrap boolean true Wrap navigation at end control.scroll-on-focus boolean true Scroll to focused element control.click-delay number 0 Delay before clicks (ms) control.focus-color string "#0066ff" Focus outline color control.focus-size number 3 Focus outline width (px) control.focus-animation boolean true Animate focus transitions control.focus-glow boolean true Add glow effect control.sound-on-focus string "none" Sound on focus change control.selector-strategy string "id-first" Element selector strategy control.refocus-timeout number 2000 Refocus timeout (ms) control.verbose boolean true Terminal announcements control.verbose-logging boolean false Browser console logging

docs.title: Installation
docs.text: This comprehensive guide will walk you through installing Inspekt on your system, from installing Python dependencies to setting up the browser userscript and verifying everything works correctly.

docs.title: Installation Flow
docs.text:
flowchart LR
    A[Install CLI] --> B[Install Userscript]
    B --> C[Start Server]
    C --> D[Test Connection]
    D --> E[Ready!]

    style A fill:#e1f5ff
    style B fill:#fff4e1
    style C fill:#ffe1f5
    style D fill:#fff9e6
    style E fill:#e1ffe1

docs.title: Requirements
docs.text:
Before you begin, ensure you have the following:

  • Python 3.11 or higher - Check your version with python --version or python3 --version
  • pip - Python package manager (usually included with Python)
  • A modern browser - Chrome, Firefox, Edge, Safari, or any Chromium-based browser
  • A userscript manager extension - We'll install this in the browser setup step

Python Version Check

Run python3 --version to check your Python version. If you have Python 3.10 or lower, you'll need to upgrade to Python 3.11 or higher.

macOSUbuntu/DebianWindows 
# Using Homebrew
brew install python@3.11

sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3.11 python3.11-pip

Download from python.org and install Python 3.11+

docs.title: Step 1: Install the CLI Tool
docs.text:
You can install Inspekt from source (recommended for development) or via pip (when available).

From Source (Recommended)Install Dependencies ManuallyFor Development

Clone the repository and install in development mode:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/roelvangils/inspekt.git
cd inspekt

# Install in development mode
pip install -e .

This installs the inspekt command and all dependencies. The -e flag means "editable" - changes to the source code will be reflected immediately.

If you prefer to manage dependencies yourself:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/roelvangils/inspekt.git
cd inspekt

# Install dependencies
pip install -r requirements.txt

If you plan to contribute or run tests:

# Clone the repository
git clone https://github.com/roelvangils/inspekt.git
cd inspekt

# Install with dev dependencies
pip install -e ".[dev]"

This includes testing tools (pytest, playwright), linters (ruff), and type checkers (mypy).

docs.title: Verify the Installation
docs.text:
After installation, verify the inspekt command is available:

inspekt--version

You should see output like:

Inspekt v2.0.0

Run the help command to see available commands:

inspekt--help

Installation Complete

The CLI tool is now installed! Next, we'll enable shell completion for a better experience.

docs.title: Step 1.5: Enable Shell Completion (Recommended)
docs.text: Shell completion enables tab-completion for all Inspekt commands, options, and arguments. This makes the CLI much faster and easier to use.

docs.title: Quick Install
docs.text:
The easiest way to enable completion is with the install command:

inspekt completion install

This auto-detects your shell (bash, zsh, or fish) and adds the completion script to your shell configuration file.

Example output:

Detected shell: zsh
Completion installed to /Users/you/.zshrc

Reload with: source /Users/you/.zshrc

docs.title: Check Status
docs.text:
To see if completion is already installed:

inspekt completion status

docs.title: Manual Installation
docs.text:
If you prefer to install manually:

BashZshFish 
# Add to ~/.bashrc
inspekt completion bash >> ~/.bashrc
source ~/.bashrc

# Add to ~/.zshrc
inspekt completion zsh >> ~/.zshrc
source ~/.zshrc

# Save to completions directory
inspekt completion fish > ~/.config/fish/completions/inspekt.fish

docs.title: Available Completion Commands
docs.text: Command Description inspekt completion install Auto-detect shell and install completion inspekt completion install -s zsh Install for specific shell inspekt completion install --force Reinstall (overwrite existing) inspekt completion status Check if completion is installed inspekt completion uninstall Remove completion from config inspekt completion bash Output bash completion script inspekt completion zsh Output zsh completion script inspekt completion fish Output fish completion script

docs.title: What Gets Completed?
docs.text:
With shell completion enabled, you can tab-complete:

  • Commands: inspekt rec<TAB> → inspekt record
  • Subcommands: inspekt record l<TAB> → inspekt record list
  • Options: inspekt replay --<TAB> → shows all available options
  • Recording files: inspekt replay rec<TAB> → completes recording_*.yaml files
  • Plugin names: inspekt plugin run <TAB> → shows available plugins

Restart Your Shell

After installing completion, restart your terminal or run source ~/.zshrc (or equivalent) to activate it.

docs.title: Step 2: Install the Browser Component
docs.text:
The browser needs a component to receive commands from the CLI and establish a WebSocket connection to the server.

Choose one installation method:

  • Extension (Recommended) - Works on ALL websites including GitHub, Gmail, banking sites. Bypasses CSP restrictions.
  • Userscript (Quick Setup) - One-click installation, but may be blocked by CSP on some sites.

docs.title: Extension Installation
docs.text: The Firefox extension provides full compatibility with all websites, including those with strict Content Security Policy (CSP) like GitHub, Gmail, and banking sites.

docs.title: 2.1a Install Firefox Extension
docs.text:
1. Download the extension files from the repository: 

    cd /path/to/inspekt
cd extensions/firefox

  2. Open Firefox and navigate to: 

    about:debugging#/runtime/this-firefox

  3. Load the extension:

  4. Click "Load Temporary Add-on…"

  5. Select the manifest.json file from extensions/firefox/

  6. Verify installation:

  7. Look for the ⚡ icon in your toolbar
  8. Click it to see the status panel

Extension Installed

The extension will now work on all websites! Continue to Step 3: Start the Bridge Server.

Why Use the Extension?

The extension bypasses Content Security Policy (CSP) restrictions that block the userscript on important sites:

  • ✅ Works on GitHub, Gmail, banking sites
  • ✅ Built-in settings panel with connection status
  • ✅ No CSP limitations

Read more about extensions →

docs.title: Userscript Installation
docs.text: The userscript is quick to install but may be blocked by CSP on some websites. If you encounter issues on GitHub, Gmail, or banking sites, use the extension instead.

docs.title: 2.1b Install a Userscript Manager
docs.text:
First, install a userscript manager extension in your browser:

Violentmonkey (Recommended)TampermonkeyGreasemonkey (Firefox only)

Best compatibility and open source.

  • Chrome/Edge
  • Firefox
  • Safari

Popular alternative with many features.

  • Chrome/Edge
  • Firefox
  • Safari

Classic Firefox userscript manager.

  • Firefox

Browser Compatibility

Inspekt works with any browser that supports userscript managers and WebSockets. This includes all modern browsers.

CSP Limitations

The userscript may be blocked by Content Security Policy on sites like:

  • GitHub, GitLab
  • Gmail, Outlook
  • Banking and government sites

If you encounter CSP issues, use the Firefox extension instead for full compatibility.

Read CSP troubleshooting guide →

docs.title: 2.2b Get the Userscript Code
docs.text:
Display the userscript code using the CLI:

inspektuserscript

This will output the complete userscript code to your terminal. The userscript is located at /Users/roelvangils/inspekt_bridge/userscript_ws.js in the repository.

docs.title: 2.3b Create the Userscript
docs.text:
Now create a new userscript in your userscript manager:

  1. Click the userscript manager icon in your browser toolbar
  2. Create a new script (usually a "+" or "New Script" button)
  3. Delete any default content in the editor
  4. Paste the userscript code from the inspektuserscript command
  5. Save the script (usually Ctrl+S or Cmd+S)

The userscript will automatically enable itself.

Quick Copy

To copy the userscript to your clipboard (macOS): 

inspektuserscript | pbcopy

Or save it to a file: 

inspektuserscript > my-userscript.js

docs.title: 2.4b Verify Userscript is Active
docs.text:
To verify the userscript is running:

  1. Open your browser's Developer Console (F12 or Cmd+Option+I)
  2. Look for a message like: "Inspekt userscript loaded"
  3. Check that the userscript manager shows the script as enabled

Userscript Scope

By default, the userscript runs on all pages (@match *://*/*). If you want to restrict it to specific domains, edit the @match line in the userscript.

docs.title: Step 3: Start the Bridge Server
docs.text: The bridge server acts as a middleman between the CLI and browser, managing WebSocket connections and HTTP endpoints.

docs.title: 3.1 Start the Server
docs.text:
You can start the server in foreground or background mode:

Background Mode (Daemon)Foreground Mode

Recommended for normal use:

inspektserver start --daemon

The server runs in the background. You can close your terminal and it will keep running.

Check server status: 

inspektserver status

Stop the server: 

inspektserver stop

Useful for debugging:

inspektserver start

The server runs in the foreground with live log output. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

Example output: 

Starting Inspekt WebSocket server...
HTTP API server: http://127.0.0.1:8765
WebSocket server: ws://127.0.0.1:8766
Server is ready! Waiting for browser connections...

docs.title: 3.2 Server Ports
docs.text:
The server uses two ports:

  • HTTP API: http://127.0.0.1:8765 - CLI communicates with this
  • WebSocket: ws://127.0.0.1:8766 - Browser connects to this

Port Configuration

The ports are currently hardcoded. If you need to change them, you'll need to modify the server configuration and userscript.

docs.title: 3.3 Verify Server is Running
docs.text:
Check the server status:

inspektserver status

Expected output when running:

✓ Server is running
  PID: 12345
  HTTP API: http://127.0.0.1:8765
  WebSocket: ws://127.0.0.1:8766
  Connected browsers: 0
  Uptime: 2 minutes

docs.title: Step 4: Verify the Complete Setup
docs.text: Now let's verify that everything is working together:

docs.title: 4.1 Open a Browser Tab
docs.text:
1. Open your browser (with the userscript manager and userscript installed)
  2. Navigate to any website, for example: https://example.com
  3. Keep the tab active (the userscript only works in active tabs)

docs.title: 4.2 Check Browser Connection
docs.text:
In the browser's Developer Console (F12), you should see:

Inspekt userscript loaded
Connected to Inspekt WebSocket server

docs.title: 4.3 Execute a Test Command
docs.text:
From your terminal, run a simple command:

inspekteval "document.title"

Expected output:

Example Domain

If you see the page title, congratulations! Everything is working correctly.

Connection Successful!

Your terminal is now connected to your browser. You can execute JavaScript directly in the active tab!

docs.title: 4.4 Try More Commands
docs.text:
# Get page information
inspektinfo

# Get the current URL
inspekteval "location.href"

# Count links on the page
inspekteval "document.querySelectorAll('a').length"

# Start interactive REPL
inspektrepl

Setup Complete!

You've successfully installed Inspekt! Check out the Quick Start Guide for a hands-on tutorial.

docs.title: "inspekt: command not found"
docs.text:
Problem: The inspekt command is not in your PATH.

Solutions:

Check InstallationUpdate PATHUse python -m 
# Verify installation
pip show inspekt

# Reinstall if needed
pip install -e .

# Find where pip installs scripts
python3 -m site --user-base

# Add to PATH (add to ~/.bashrc or ~/.zshrc)
export PATH="$PATH:$(python3 -m site --user-base)/bin"

# Run as a module instead
python3 -m inspekt.cli --help

docs.title: "Bridge server is not running"
docs.text:
Problem: The CLI cannot connect to the server.

Solutions:

  1. Start the server: 

    inspektserver start --daemon

  2. Check if server is running: 

    inspektserver status

  3. Restart the server: 

    inspektserver stop
inspektserver start --daemon

  4. Check for port conflicts: 

    # Check if ports 8765 or 8766 are in use
lsof -i :8765
lsof -i :8766

docs.title: "No response from browser"
docs.text:
Problem: The browser is not connected to the WebSocket server.

Solutions:

  1. Verify userscript is installed and enabled
  2. Check userscript manager icon

  3. Ensure script is enabled

  4. Check browser console for errors

  5. Open DevTools (F12)
  6. Look for WebSocket connection errors

  7. Ensure you see "Connected to Inspekt WebSocket server"

  8. Ensure tab is active

  9. The userscript only works in the currently active browser tab

  10. Switch to the tab and try again

  11. Restart everything: 

    # Stop server
inspektserver stop

# Restart browser (to reload userscript)

# Start server
inspektserver start --daemon

  12. Check WebSocket connection manually

  13. In browser console, run: 
    ws = new WebSocket('ws://127.0.0.1:8766')
ws.onopen = () => console.log('Connected!')

docs.title: Command Timeout
docs.text:
Problem: Commands hang or timeout.

Solutions:

  1. Increase timeout: 

    inspekteval "slow_operation()" --timeout 30

  2. Check if tab is active:

  3. Inactive tabs may throttle JavaScript execution

  4. Switch to the tab and try again

  5. Check for JavaScript errors:

  6. Open browser console
  7. Look for errors when command executes

docs.title: WebSocket Connection Refused
docs.text:
Problem: Browser cannot connect to WebSocket server.

Solutions:

  1. Verify server is running: 

    inspektserver status

  2. Check firewall settings:

  3. Ensure localhost connections are allowed

  4. Port 8766 must be accessible

  5. Try a different port (requires code modification):

  6. Edit server configuration
  7. Update userscript to match

docs.title: Python Version Issues
docs.text:
Problem: Inspekt requires Python 3.11+, but you have an older version.

Solution: Upgrade Python:

macOS (Homebrew)Ubuntu/DebianWindows 
brew install python@3.11
# Update PATH in ~/.zshrc or ~/.bashrc
export PATH="/usr/local/opt/python@3.11/bin:$PATH"

sudo apt update
sudo apt install python3.11 python3.11-pip
# Use python3.11 explicitly
python3.11 -m pip install -e .

Download and install from python.org

docs.title: Uninstallation
docs.text: To uninstall Inspekt:

docs.title: 1. Stop the Server
docs.text: inspektserver stop

docs.title: 2. Uninstall the Package
docs.text:
# If installed with pip
pip uninstall inspekt

# If installed from source, just delete the directory
rm -rf ~/inspekt

docs.title: 3. Remove Browser Userscript
docs.text:
1. Click userscript manager icon
  2. Find "Inspekt" script
  3. Delete or disable the script

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
Now that you have Inspekt installed, continue with:

  • Quick Start Guide - 5-minute hands-on tutorial
  • Configuration - Customize your setup
  • User Guide - Learn all commands and features

docs.title: Additional Resources
docs.text:
• GitHub Repository - Source code and issues
  • Architecture Guide - How Inspekt works internally
  • Security Guide - Security model and best practices

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
Get up and running with Inspekt in just 5 minutes! This hands-on tutorial will walk you through the basics and show you the power of browser automation from the command line.

Prerequisites

Make sure you've completed the Installation guide before starting this tutorial.

Enable Shell Completion

For a better experience, enable tab completion: 

inspekt completion install
This lets you tab-complete commands, options, and file arguments. See Shell Completion for details.

docs.title: Quick Start Workflow
docs.text:
Here's what we'll cover in this tutorial:

graph LR
    A[Execute JavaScript] --> B[Use REPL]
    B --> C[Extract Data]
    C --> D[Automate Tasks]
    D --> E[Advanced Features]

    style A fill:#e1f5ff
    style B fill:#fff4e1
    style C fill:#ffe1f5
    style D fill:#fff9e6
    style E fill:#e1ffe1

docs.title: Step 1: Navigate to a Test Page
docs.text: Open your browser and navigate to https://example.com. Keep this tab active.

docs.title: Step 2: Execute JavaScript
docs.text:
Run your first command to get the page title:

inspekteval "document.title"

Expected output:

Example Domain

Congratulations! You just executed JavaScript in your browser from the terminal.

docs.title: Step 3: Try More Expressions
docs.text:
# Get the current URL
inspekteval "location.href"
# => https://example.com/

# Count paragraphs on the page
inspekteval "document.querySelectorAll('p').length"
# => 2

# Get all link URLs
inspekteval "Array.from(document.links).map(a => a.href)"
# => ["https://www.iana.org/domains/example"]

Quick Tip

The inspekteval command evaluates JavaScript expressions. For more complex code, use inspektexec with a file.

docs.title: Interactive REPL Session
docs.text:
The REPL (Read-Eval-Print Loop) lets you experiment with JavaScript interactively:

inspektrepl

Try these commands in the REPL:

// Get the page title
inspekt> document.title
"Example Domain"

// Query the DOM
inspekt> document.querySelectorAll('h1')[0].textContent
"Example Domain"

// Create an array of links
inspekt> Array.from(document.links).map(a => ({text: a.textContent, href: a.href}))
[{text: "More information…", href: "https://www.iana.org/domains/example"}]

// Exit the REPL
inspekt> exit
Goodbye!

REPL Power

The REPL is perfect for exploring APIs, debugging, and prototyping JavaScript code before adding it to scripts.

docs.title: Extract Page Information
docs.text:
Use the info command to get comprehensive page details:

inspektinfo

Example output:

URL:      https://example.com
Title:    Example Domain
Domain:   example.com
Protocol: https:
State:    complete
Size:     1280x720

For extended information including language, meta tags, and cookies:

inspektinfo --extended

docs.title: Working with Links
docs.text: Navigate to a page with more links (like a news site or blog), then:

docs.title: List All Links
docs.text:
inspektlinks

Example output:

→ Home Page
  https://example.com/

→ About Us
  https://example.com/about

↗ External Resource
  https://other-site.com/page

Total: 15 links (12 internal, 3 external)

docs.title: Extract External Links Only
docs.text:
inspektlinks --only-external --only-urls

This outputs just the URLs, one per line - perfect for piping to other tools.

docs.title: Save Links to a File
docs.text: inspektlinks --only-urls > all-links.txt

docs.title: Get Enriched Link Metadata
docs.text:
inspektlinks --only-external --enrich-external

This fetches additional metadata like MIME types, file sizes, and HTTP status codes.

docs.title: Click an Element
docs.text:
# Click by CSS selector
inspektclick "button#submit"

# Double-click
inspektdouble-click "div.editable"

# Right-click (context menu)
inspektright-click "a.download"

docs.title: Highlight Elements
docs.text:
Useful for visual debugging:

# Highlight all headings
inspekthighlight "h1, h2, h3"

# Custom color
inspekthighlight "a" --color blue

# Clear highlights
inspekthighlight --clear

docs.title: Wait for Elements
docs.text:
Perfect for automation:

# Wait for element to exist (default: 30s timeout)
inspektwait "button#submit"

# Wait for element to be visible
inspektwait ".modal-dialog" --visible

# Wait for element to be hidden
inspektwait ".loading-spinner" --hidden

# Wait for text content
inspektwait "div.result" --text "Success"

# Custom timeout (10 seconds)
inspektwait "div.notification" --timeout 10

docs.title: View Heading Hierarchy
docs.text:
inspektoutline

Example output:

H1 Getting Started
   H2 Installation
      H3 Prerequisites
      H3 Setup
   H2 Configuration
      H3 Basic Settings
      H3 Advanced Options
         H4 Environment Variables

Total: 7 headings

This is great for:

  • Accessibility audits
  • SEO analysis
  • Understanding page structure

docs.title: Extract Table Data
docs.text: inspektexec inspekt/scripts/extract_table.js --format json > data.json

docs.title: Extract All Images
docs.text: inspektexec inspekt/scripts/extract_images.js --format json

docs.title: Get SEO Metadata
docs.text: inspektexec inspekt/scripts/extract_metadata.js --format json

docs.title: Custom Extraction
docs.text:
Extract product prices (example):

inspekteval "
  Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.product')).map(p => ({
    name: p.querySelector('.name').textContent,
    price: p.querySelector('.price').textContent
  }))
" --format json

Format Options

Use --format json for structured output, --format raw for plain text, or --format default for human-readable output.

docs.title: AI-Powered Features
docs.text:
Requires mods

AI features require mods to be installed.

docs.title: Summarize an Article
docs.text:
Navigate to a news article or blog post, then:

inspektsummarize

This extracts the article content using Mozilla Readability and generates a concise summary.

docs.title: Describe a Page for Screen Readers
docs.text:
inspektdescribe

Example output:

This webpage is in English. At the top you can navigate to Home, About,
Services, and Contact. The main part contains an article about browser
automation with three headings. The footer contains links to Privacy
Policy and Terms of Service.

Perfect for understanding page structure before diving into automation.

docs.title: Form Automation Example
docs.text:
Let's automate filling out a login form:

# Fill email field
inspekteval "document.querySelector('#email').value = 'user@example.com'"

# Fill password field
inspekteval "document.querySelector('#password').value = 'mypassword'"

# Click submit button
inspektclick "button[type=submit]"

# Wait for success message
inspektwait ".success-message" --visible

# Verify we're logged in
inspekteval "document.querySelector('.user-name').textContent"

Security Note

Be careful with passwords in command history! See the Security Guide for best practices.

docs.title: Navigation Commands
docs.text:
# Navigate to a URL
inspektopen https://example.com

# Navigate and wait for page load
inspektopen https://example.com --wait

# Go back in history
inspektback

# Go forward in history
inspektforward

# Reload the page
inspektreload

# Hard reload (bypass cache)
inspektreload --hard

docs.title: Get Selected Text
docs.text:
Select some text in the browser, then:

# Get selected text with metadata
inspektselected

# Raw text only
inspektselected --raw

# Copy to clipboard (macOS)
inspektselected --raw | pbcopy

docs.title: Send Text to Browser
docs.text:
Type text character by character into focused field:

# Type into currently focused field
inspektsend "Hello World"

# Type into specific field
inspektsend "test@example.com" --selector "input[type=email]"

docs.title: Keyboard Control Mode
docs.text:
Navigate pages entirely with your keyboard:

inspektcontrol

Controls:

  • Tab / Shift+Tab - Navigate forward/backward
  • Up Down Left Right - Move focus directionally
  • Enter / Space - Activate focused element
  • Esc - Return to body
  • Q - Quit control mode

Features:

  • Auto-refocus after page navigation
  • Visual feedback (blue outlines)
  • Real-time terminal announcements
  • Optional text-to-speech (macOS)

Control Mode Configuration

Customize control mode behavior in config.json. See the Configuration Guide.

docs.title: Watch Browser Events
docs.text:
Monitor keyboard input in real-time:

inspektwatch input

Focus any text field in the browser and start typing. The terminal will show each keystroke:

Watching keyboard input... (Press Ctrl+C to stop)
H e l l o [SPACE] W o r l d [ENTER]

Press Ctrl+C to stop watching.

docs.title: Execute JavaScript from Files
docs.text:
Create a file extract-titles.js:

// Extract all headings from the page
const headings = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h1, h2, h3, h4, h5, h6'))
  .map(h => ({
    level: h.tagName,
    text: h.textContent.trim(),
    id: h.id
  }));

headings;  // Return value

Execute it:

inspektexec extract-titles.js --format json

Or use the shorthand:

inspektexec extract-titles.js --format json
# Same as:
inspekteval --file extract-titles.js --format json

docs.title: Working with Output Formats
docs.text:
Inspekt supports multiple output formats:

Default (Human-Readable)JSONRaw 
inspekteval "({title: document.title, url: location.href})"

Output: 

{
  title: "Example Domain",
  url: "https://example.com/"
}


inspekteval "({title: document.title, url: location.href})" --format json

Output: 

{
  "title": "Example Domain",
  "url": "https://example.com/"
}


inspekteval "document.title" --format raw

Output: 

Example Domain

No extra formatting - perfect for piping to other commands.

docs.title: Combining with Shell Commands
docs.text:
Inspekt plays nicely with standard Unix tools:

# Count external links
inspektlinks --only-external --only-urls | wc -l

# Find all PDF links
inspektlinks --only-urls | grep "\.pdf$"

# Get unique domains from external links
inspektlinks --only-external --only-urls | sed 's|https\?://\([^/]*\).*|\1|' | sort | uniq

# Export data and process with jq
inspekteval "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a')).map(a => ({text: a.textContent, href: a.href}))" --format json | jq '.[0:5]'

docs.title: Check if Element Exists
docs.text:
inspekteval "document.querySelector('#element-id') !== null"
# => true or false

docs.title: Get Computed Style
docs.text:
inspekteval "getComputedStyle(document.querySelector('h1')).color"
# => rgb(0, 0, 0)

docs.title: Scroll to Bottom

docs.title: Practice Challenges
docs.text:
Try these exercises to build your skills:

Challenge 1: Link Analysis

Navigate to your favorite news site and:

  1. Count total links on the homepage
  2. Extract all external links
  3. Find all links containing "privacy" or "terms"
  4. Save results to a file
Solution 
# 1. Count total links
inspekteval "document.querySelectorAll('a').length"

# 2. Extract external links
inspektlinks --only-external --only-urls > external.txt

# 3. Find privacy/terms links
inspektlinks --only-urls | grep -E "(privacy|terms)"

# 4. Already saved in step 2!

Challenge 2: Form Automation

Find a demo contact form online and:

  1. Fill all fields programmatically
  2. Submit the form
  3. Wait for success message
  4. Extract the success message text
Solution 
# 1. Fill fields
inspekteval "document.querySelector('#name').value = 'John Doe'"
inspekteval "document.querySelector('#email').value = 'john@example.com'"
inspekteval "document.querySelector('#message').value = 'Hello!'"

# 2. Submit
inspektclick "button[type=submit]"

# 3. Wait for success
inspektwait ".success-message" --visible

# 4. Extract message
inspekteval "document.querySelector('.success-message').textContent"

Challenge 3: Data Extraction

Navigate to a Wikipedia article and:

  1. Get the article title
  2. Count all sections (h2 headings)
  3. Extract all image URLs
  4. Create JSON with all the data
Solution 
# 1. Get title
inspekteval "document.querySelector('h1').textContent"

# 2. Count sections
inspekteval "document.querySelectorAll('h2').length"

# 3. Extract images
inspekteval "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('img')).map(img => img.src)"

# 4. Create JSON
inspekteval "{
  title: document.querySelector('h1').textContent,
  sections: document.querySelectorAll('h2').length,
  images: Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('img')).map(img => img.src)
}" --format json > wikipedia.json
