docs.title: Shell Completion
docs.text: Inspekt provides intelligent tab completion for all commands, options, and arguments. This guide covers how to set up completions for your terminal.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Inspekt uses Click's built-in shell completion, which queries the live CLI at runtime—so completions are always in sync with the installed version.

Terminals Sync Features Bash, Zsh, Fish, Ghostty, iTerm2, VS Code, Warp Automatic Dynamic completions from live CLI

docs.title: Shell Completion (Bash, Zsh, Fish)
docs.text: This is the recommended completion system for most terminals. It uses Click's built-in completion mechanism, which queries the live CLI at runtime—so completions are always in sync with the installed version.

docs.title: Quick Install
docs.text:
The fastest way to set up completion:

inspekt completion install

This auto-detects your shell and adds completion to your config file.

docs.title: Manual Installation
docs.text:
If you prefer manual setup or the auto-install doesn't work:

BashZshFish

Add to your ~/.bashrc:

eval "$(_INSPEKT_COMPLETE=bash_source inspekt)"

Then reload: 

source ~/.bashrc

Add to your ~/.zshrc:

eval "$(_INSPEKT_COMPLETE=zsh_source inspekt)"

Then reload: 

source ~/.zshrc

Add to ~/.config/fish/completions/inspekt.fish:

_INSPEKT_COMPLETE=fish_source inspekt | source

Fish will auto-load completions from this directory.

docs.title: Check Installation Status
docs.text:
inspekt completion status

Example output:

┌─ Shell Completion ──────────────────────────────┐
│ Shell    │ zsh                                  │
│ Config   │ /Users/you/.zshrc                    │
│ Status   │ ✓ Installed                          │
└──────────────────────────────────────────────────┘

docs.title: Uninstall
docs.text: inspekt completion uninstall

docs.title: Command Completion
docs.text:
Type inspekt and press Tab to see all available commands:

inspekt <TAB>
# Shows: ask, axe, back, bottom, click, completion, config, console, ...

docs.title: Option Completion
docs.text:
After a command, press Tab to see available options:

inspekt record --<TAB>
# Shows: --output, --replay, --open, --no-hover, --capture-state, ...

docs.title: Argument Completion
docs.text:
Some arguments have dynamic completion:

# Recording files are auto-completed
inspekt replay rec<TAB>
# Shows: recording_20231215_login.yaml, recording_20231214_checkout.yaml, ...

# Shell types for completion install
inspekt completion install -s <TAB>
# Shows: bash, zsh, fish

docs.title: Choice Completion
docs.text:
Options with predefined choices show suggestions:

inspekt axe --level <TAB>
# Shows: 2a, 2aa, 2aaa, 21a, 21aa, 22aa

inspekt type --speed <TAB>
# Shows: instant, fast, normal, slow

docs.title: Ghostty
docs.text: Ghostty uses your shell's completion system. Follow the Shell Completion instructions for your shell.

docs.title: iTerm2
docs.text: iTerm2 uses your shell's completion system. Follow the Shell Completion instructions for your shell.

docs.title: VS Code Integrated Terminal
docs.text: VS Code's terminal uses your shell's completion system. Make sure completion is installed for your shell, then restart VS Code.

docs.title: Warp
docs.text:
Warp uses your shell's completion system. Follow the Shell Completion instructions for your shell.

Warp Keyboard Shortcuts

In Warp, trigger completions with:

  • Tab - Standard completion
  • Ctrl+Space - Force show completions
  • Up / Down - Navigate suggestions

docs.title: How Shell Completion Works
docs.text:
Understanding the mechanism helps with troubleshooting:

sequenceDiagram
    participant User
    participant Shell
    participant Inspekt

    User->>Shell: Types "inspekt rec<TAB>"
    Shell->>Inspekt: Runs with _INSPEKT_COMPLETE=zsh_source
    Inspekt->>Inspekt: Introspects Click commands
    Inspekt->>Shell: Returns matching completions
    Shell->>User: Shows "record", "reload", "replay", "repl", "restart"
  1. You type inspekt rec and press Tab
  2. Your shell detects the completion request
  3. Shell runs _INSPEKT_COMPLETE=zsh_source inspekt
  4. Inspekt returns matching completions based on Click's command definitions
  5. Shell displays the suggestions

This is why shell completion is always in sync—it queries the live CLI every time.

docs.title: Completions Not Working
docs.text:
1. Check if installed: 

    inspekt completion status

  2. Reload your shell config: 

    source ~/.zshrc  # or ~/.bashrc

  3. Restart your terminal to ensure changes take effect

docs.title: Slow Completions
docs.text: If completions feel slow, it's because the CLI is invoked on each Tab. This is normal for complex CLIs—caching isn't possible with dynamic completions.

docs.title: Wrong Completions After Update
docs.text:
If you're seeing old completions after updating Inspekt, just reload your shell:

source ~/.zshrc  # or ~/.bashrc

docs.title: inspekt completion install
docs.text:
Auto-detect shell and install completion.

inspekt completion install           # Auto-detect shell
inspekt completion install -s zsh    # Specify shell
inspekt completion install --force   # Reinstall

docs.title: inspekt completion uninstall
docs.text:
Remove completion from your shell config.

inspekt completion uninstall
inspekt completion uninstall -s bash

docs.title: inspekt completion status
docs.text:
Check if completion is installed.

inspekt completion status

docs.title: Shell-specific scripts
docs.text:
Output raw completion scripts for manual installation:

inspekt completion bash    # Bash script
inspekt completion zsh     # Zsh script
inspekt completion fish    # Fish script

docs.title: Updating Inspekt
docs.text: Keep Inspekt up to date to get the latest features, bug fixes, and improvements.

docs.title: Updating the CLI
docs.text: The Inspekt CLI is installed via pip and can be updated with a single command.

docs.title: Check Current Version
docs.text: inspekt--version

docs.title: Update to Latest Version
docs.text:
pip install --upgrade inspekt-bridge

Or with pipx:

pipx upgrade inspekt-bridge

docs.title: Verify Update
docs.text:
inspekt--version
# Should show the new version

inspektserver restart
# Restart the server to use the new version

docs.title: Updating the Userscript
docs.text: The userscript runs in your browser and needs to be updated separately from the CLI.

docs.title: Automatic Updates (Recommended)
docs.text:
Since version 3.5, the userscript supports automatic updates:

  1. Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey will check for updates periodically (usually daily)
  2. You'll be prompted when an update is available
  3. Click "Update" to install the new version

To check manually:

  1. Open Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey dashboard
  2. Find "Inspekt (WebSocket)"
  3. Click the "Check for updates" button
  4. Install if an update is available

docs.title: Manual Update
docs.text:
If you have version 3.4 or earlier (without auto-update):

  1. Open Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey dashboard
  2. Delete the old "Inspekt" script
  3. Visit the raw userscript file: 
    https://raw.githubusercontent.com/roelvangils/inspekt-bridge/main/userscript_ws.js
  4. Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey will prompt to install the new version
  5. Click "Install"
  6. Reload any open tabs to activate the new version

docs.title: Verify Userscript Version
docs.text:
Open the browser console (F12) and check:

window.__INSPEKT_BRIDGE_VERSION__
// Should show "3.5" or higher

Or look for the version in the console on page load:

[Inspekt] Connected via WebSocket

docs.title: Version 3.5 (Latest)
docs.text:
New Features: - ✅ CSP (Content Security Policy) detection - ✅ User-friendly warnings when CSP blocks Zen - ✅ Automatic update support via @updateURL - ✅ Better error handling for connection failures

Changes: - Prevents unnecessary reconnection attempts on CSP-blocked sites - Exposes __INSPEKT_BRIDGE_CSP_BLOCKED__ flag for CLI integration

Documentation: - New troubleshooting guide for CSP issues - Comprehensive explanation of CSP limitations

docs.title: Version 3.4
docs.text: Features: - WebSocket-based communication - DevTools integration with inspektStore($0) - Keepalive ping/pong - Auto-reconnection on disconnect - Visibility-based connection management

docs.title: Version 3.x → 4.x (If/When Released)
docs.text: Future major versions may include breaking changes. Check the changelog before updating.

docs.title: Version 2.x → 3.x (Historical)
docs.text:
• Switched from HTTP polling to WebSocket
  • Changed server ports (8765 HTTP API, 8766 WebSocket)
  • Improved reconnection logic

docs.title: CLI Update Issues
docs.text:
Issue: "Command not found" after update

# If using pip
which inspekt
# Should show path to inspekt

# If it's missing, reinstall
pip install --force-reinstall inspekt-bridge

# If using pipx
pipx reinstall inspekt-bridge

Issue: Old version still showing

# Clear pip cache
pip cache purge

# Reinstall
pip install --upgrade --force-reinstall --no-cache-dir inspekt-bridge

# Verify
inspekt--version

docs.title: Userscript Update Issues
docs.text:
Issue: Auto-update not working

You may have version 3.4 or earlier without auto-update support. Use the manual update method above.

Issue: Two versions installed

  1. Open Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey dashboard
  2. Look for duplicate "Inspekt" entries
  3. Delete the older version (check version number in script header)
  4. Keep only the latest version

Issue: "Script already installed" error

  1. Delete the existing script first
  2. Then install the new version
  3. Reload browser tabs

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
Check the GitHub Releases page for new versions:

# Check PyPI for latest version
pip index versions inspekt-bridge

# Compare with your version
inspekt--version

docs.title: Userscript
docs.text:
The userscript version is in the file header:

// @version      3.5

Check the latest version on GitHub.

docs.title: Stay Informed
docs.text:
• Watch the repository on GitHub for release notifications
  • Star the repo to follow development
  • Check the changelog regularly: CHANGELOG.md

docs.title: Automatic Checks
docs.text:
The CLI doesn't currently check for updates automatically. This may be added in a future version.

The userscript (v3.5+) automatically checks for updates via Tampermonkey/Violentmonkey.

docs.title: Downgrading
docs.text: If you need to downgrade due to issues:

docs.title: CLI
docs.text:
# Downgrade to specific version
pip install inspekt-bridge==2.0.0

# Or use pipx
pipx install inspekt-bridge==2.0.0 --force

docs.title: Userscript
docs.text:
1. Visit the commit history
  2. Find the version you want
  3. Click "View file" on that commit
  4. Click "Raw" to get the direct URL
  5. Install from that URL

docs.title: Best Practices
docs.text:
1. Always update both CLI and userscript together for compatibility
  2. Restart the server after CLI updates: inspektserver restart
  3. Reload browser tabs after userscript updates
  4. Check the changelog before updating for breaking changes
  5. Test after updates to ensure everything works

docs.title: Need Help?
docs.text:
If you encounter issues during updates:

  1. Check the Troubleshooting Guide
  2. Visit GitHub Issues
  3. Include your version numbers when reporting problems: 
    inspekt--version
# And userscript version from console

docs.title: Accessibility Testing
docs.text: Learn how to test web accessibility using Inspekt's integrated axe-core testing capabilities. Ensure your websites are accessible to all users, comply with WCAG standards, and catch accessibility issues before they reach production.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: Inspekt provides professional accessibility testing through the inspekt axe command, powered by the industry-standard axe-core library from Deque Systems - the same engine that powers Chrome DevTools Lighthouse accessibility audits.

docs.title: Why Accessibility Matters
docs.text:
Legal compliance: - ADA (Americans with Disabilities Act) - Section 508 (US Federal) - EN 301 549 (European Union) - AODA (Ontario, Canada) - Many countries require WCAG 2.0 or 2.1 Level AA

Business benefits: - 15% of global population has some form of disability - Better SEO (accessible sites rank higher) - Improved usability for everyone - Reduced legal risk - Enhanced brand reputation

Technical benefits: - Better semantic HTML structure - Improved keyboard navigation - Clearer content hierarchy - More maintainable code

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Navigate to any page
inspekt open https://example.com

# Run accessibility audit
inspekt axe

# View results

Example output: 

┌─────────────────┬──────────┬───────┬──────────────────────────┐
│ Rule            │ Impact   │ Count │ Description              │
├─────────────────┼──────────┼───────┼──────────────────────────┤
│ color-contrast  │ serious  │ 12    │ Ensure sufficient cont...│
│ image-alt       │ critical │ 3     │ Images must have alt...  │
│ label           │ serious  │ 5     │ Form elements must...    │
└─────────────────┴──────────┴───────┴──────────────────────────┘

Summary: 3 violations (1 critical, 2 serious)
Passes: 45

That's it! You now have a comprehensive accessibility audit of your page.

docs.title: Test Authenticated Content
docs.text:
Unlike browser extensions or standalone tools, Inspekt tests your current browser state:

# You log in manually, navigate to dashboard
inspekt open https://app.example.com
# (Log in through browser UI)

# Audit your actual authenticated session
inspekt axe --level 21aa

# Continue to other logged-in pages
inspekt axe

Test areas other tools can't reach: - User dashboards - Account settings - Admin panels - Private content - Checkout flows - Form validation states

docs.title: Test Dynamic States
docs.text:
Test accessibility at any point in your user journey:

# Test search results after filtering
inspekt open https://store.example.com
# Apply filters in browser (price range, category, etc.)
inspekt axe

# Test modal dialogs
# Click to open modal
inspekt axe  # Tests modal in open state

# Test form error states
# Submit form with validation errors
inspekt axe  # Tests error messages, ARIA live regions

docs.title: Continuous Testing Workflow
docs.text:
# 1. Navigate to feature
inspekt open http://localhost:3000/new-feature

# 2. Test
inspekt axe --level 21aa

# 3. Fix issues in code

# 4. Reload
inspekt reload

# 5. Re-test
inspekt axe --level 21aa

# Repeat until clean

Fast iteration - No browser restart, no re-authentication, no navigation replay.

docs.title: Understanding WCAG Levels
docs.text: WCAG (Web Content Accessibility Guidelines) has three conformance levels:

docs.title: Level A (Minimum)
docs.text:
Basic web accessibility - most critical issues: - All images have alt text - Videos have captions - Forms have labels - Headings are in logical order - Keyboard accessible

Test with: 

inspekt axe --level 2a

docs.title: Level AA (Standard) ⭐ Recommended
docs.text:
Standard for most legal requirements: - Everything in Level A - Color contrast meets 4.5:1 ratio - Visible focus indicators - Multiple ways to find pages - Consistent navigation - Error suggestions

Test with: 

inspekt axe --level 2aa      # WCAG 2.0 AA
inspekt axe --level 21aa     # WCAG 2.1 AA (recommended)
inspekt axe --level 22aa     # WCAG 2.2 AA (latest)

Most organizations target WCAG 2.1 Level AA.

docs.title: Level AAA (Enhanced)
docs.text:
Highest level - exceeds legal requirements: - Everything in Level AA - Enhanced color contrast (7:1 ratio) - Sign language interpretation - Extended audio descriptions - Very strict requirements

Test with: 

inspekt axe --level 2aaa

Note: Level AAA is rarely required and very difficult to achieve. Most organizations aim for Level AA.

docs.title: 1. Color Contrast
docs.text:
The problem: Text doesn't have enough contrast against background.

Why it matters: Users with low vision or color blindness can't read content.

WCAG requirement: - Normal text: 4.5:1 contrast ratio (AA), 7:1 (AAA) - Large text (18pt+): 3:1 contrast ratio (AA), 4.5:1 (AAA)

How to fix: 

/* Bad - insufficient contrast */
.text {
  color: #999999;              /* Light gray */
  background-color: #FFFFFF;    /* White */
  /* Contrast: 2.8:1 ❌ */
}

/* Good - sufficient contrast */
.text {
  color: #595959;              /* Darker gray */
  background-color: #FFFFFF;    /* White */
  /* Contrast: 7:1 ✓ */
}

Testing: 

inspekt axe --level 21aa
# Look for "color-contrast" violations

# Or check ONLY color contrast issues
inspekt axe --enable-rule color-contrast

docs.title: 2. Missing Alt Text
docs.text:
The problem: Images lack alternative text.

Why it matters: Screen readers can't describe images to blind users.

How to fix: 

<!-- Bad -->
<img src="product.jpg">

<!-- Good - descriptive alt text -->
<img src="product.jpg" alt="Blue wireless headphones with noise cancellation">

<!-- Good - decorative image -->
<img src="decoration.svg" alt="" role="presentation">

Rules: - Informative images: Describe what the image shows - Functional images: Describe what happens when clicked - Decorative images: Use empty alt (alt="") - Complex images: Provide long description nearby

Testing: 

inspekt axe --level 21aa
# Look for "image-alt" violations

docs.title: 3. Form Labels
docs.text:
The problem: Input fields don't have associated labels.

Why it matters: Screen reader users don't know what to enter.

How to fix: 

<!-- Bad - no label -->
<input type="text" name="email">

<!-- Good - explicit label -->
<label for="email">Email Address</label>
<input type="text" id="email" name="email">

<!-- Good - implicit label -->
<label>
  Email Address
  <input type="text" name="email">
</label>

<!-- Good - ARIA label (use sparingly) -->
<input type="text" name="email" aria-label="Email Address">

Testing: 

inspekt axe --level 21aa
# Look for "label" violations

docs.title: 4. Keyboard Navigation
docs.text:
The problem: Interactive elements can't be accessed via keyboard.

Why it matters: Users who can't use a mouse are excluded.

Requirements: - All interactive elements must be focusable (Tab key) - Focus order must be logical - Visible focus indicator required - No keyboard traps (can Tab out)

How to fix: 

<!-- Bad - div is not keyboard accessible -->
<div onclick="handleClick()">Click me</div>

<!-- Good - button is keyboard accessible -->
<button onclick="handleClick()">Click me</button>

<!-- Good - div made accessible with role and tabindex -->
<div role="button" tabindex="0" onclick="handleClick()" onkeypress="handleClick()">
  Click me
</div>

CSS for focus indicators: 

/* Don't do this! */
*:focus {
  outline: none; /* ❌ Removes focus indicator */
}

/* Do this instead */
button:focus,
a:focus {
  outline: 2px solid #0066CC;
  outline-offset: 2px;
}

Manual testing: 

# Automated test
inspekt axe --level 21aa

# Manual keyboard test
# 1. Close your mouse/trackpad
# 2. Navigate page using only Tab, Shift+Tab, Enter, Space, Arrow keys
# 3. Verify you can reach all interactive elements
# 4. Verify you can see where focus is
# 5. Verify you can't get stuck (keyboard trap)

docs.title: 5. Heading Hierarchy
docs.text:
The problem: Heading levels skip (H1 → H3) or are out of order.

Why it matters: Screen readers use headings for navigation. Logical structure is essential.

How to fix: 

<!-- Bad - skips H2 -->
<h1>Main Page Title</h1>
<h3>Subsection</h3>  <!-- Skipped H2! -->

<!-- Good - logical hierarchy -->
<h1>Main Page Title</h1>
<h2>Major Section</h2>
<h3>Subsection</h3>
<h3>Another Subsection</h3>
<h2>Another Major Section</h2>

Rules: - One H1 per page (page title) - Don't skip levels (H1 → H3) - Headings should describe content - Visual styling ≠ heading level (use CSS)

Testing: 

# View heading structure
inspekt outline

# Check for heading-order violations
inspekt axe --level 21aa --tags best-practice

docs.title: 6. ARIA Usage
docs.text:
The problem: ARIA attributes used incorrectly or unnecessarily.

Why it matters: Broken ARIA is worse than no ARIA.

First rule of ARIA: Don't use ARIA.

Use semantic HTML instead: 

<!-- Bad - unnecessary ARIA -->
<div role="button" tabindex="0" aria-pressed="false">Click</div>

<!-- Good - semantic HTML -->
<button>Click</button>

When ARIA is needed: 

<!-- Good - Live region for dynamic updates -->
<div role="alert" aria-live="polite">
  Form submitted successfully!
</div>

<!-- Good - Expanded state for accordion -->
<button aria-expanded="false" aria-controls="panel">
  Show Details
</button>
<div id="panel" hidden>
  Details here...
</div>

Testing: 

inspekt axe --level 21aa
# Look for ARIA-related violations

docs.title: Development Workflow
docs.text:
# 1. Start development server
npm run dev

# 2. Open in browser via Inspekt
inspekt open http://localhost:3000

# 3. Run accessibility audit
inspekt axe --level 21aa

# 4. Fix violations in code

# 5. Reload browser
inspekt reload

# 6. Re-run audit
inspekt axe --level 21aa

# Repeat 4-6 until clean

docs.title: Pre-Commit Workflow
docs.text:
# Create git hook: .git/hooks/pre-commit
#!/bin/bash

echo "Running accessibility audit…"

inspekt open http://localhost:3000 --wait
RESULT=$(inspekt axe --level 21aa --json)

CRITICAL=$(echo "$RESULT" | jq '.summary.criticalCount')
SERIOUS=$(echo "$RESULT" | jq '.summary.seriousCount')

if [ "$CRITICAL" -gt 0 ]; then
    echo "❌ Critical accessibility issues found! Fix before committing."
    exit 1
fi

if [ "$SERIOUS" -gt 5 ]; then
    echo "⚠️  Warning: $SERIOUS serious accessibility issues"
fi

echo "✅ Accessibility check passed"
exit 0

docs.title: CI/CD Workflow
docs.text:
# .github/workflows/accessibility.yml
name: Accessibility Testing

on: [push, pull_request]

jobs:
  a11y-test:
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v2

      - name: Install Inspekt
        run: pip install inspekt

      - name: Start servers
        run: |
          inspekt server start
          npm run dev &
          sleep 5

      - name: Run accessibility audit
        run: |
          inspekt open http://localhost:3000 --wait
          inspekt axe --level 21aa --json > results.json

      - name: Check results
        run: |
          CRITICAL=$(jq '.summary.criticalCount' results.json)
          SERIOUS=$(jq '.summary.seriousCount' results.json)

          if [ "$CRITICAL" -gt 0 ] || [ "$SERIOUS" -gt 0 ]; then
            echo "❌ Accessibility violations found!"
            echo "Critical: $CRITICAL, Serious: $SERIOUS"
            exit 1
          fi

docs.title: Manual Testing Checklist
docs.text:
Automated tools catch ~30-40% of issues. Also test manually:

Keyboard navigation: - [ ] Tab through all interactive elements - [ ] Verify visible focus indicators - [ ] Test modals/dialogs (can you escape?) - [ ] Test dropdown menus - [ ] Test custom widgets

Screen reader testing: - [ ] Test with NVDA (Windows, free) - [ ] Test with JAWS (Windows, paid) - [ ] Test with VoiceOver (Mac, built-in) - [ ] Verify all images have meaningful alt text - [ ] Verify form labels are announced - [ ] Verify error messages are announced - [ ] Test landmark navigation

Visual testing: - [ ] Zoom to 200% (text should reflow) - [ ] Test high contrast mode - [ ] Test with color blindness simulation - [ ] Verify color is not the only indicator

Mobile testing: - [ ] Test with screen reader on mobile - [ ] Verify touch targets are 44×44 pixels minimum - [ ] Test with zoom enabled - [ ] Verify orientation (portrait/landscape)

docs.title: Regression Testing
docs.text:
Track accessibility over time:

#!/bin/bash
# Save baseline
inspekt axe --json > baseline.json

# After changes
inspekt axe --json > current.json

# Compare
BASELINE_VIOLATIONS=$(jq '.summary.violationCount' baseline.json)
CURRENT_VIOLATIONS=$(jq '.summary.violationCount' current.json)

if [ "$CURRENT_VIOLATIONS" -gt "$BASELINE_VIOLATIONS" ]; then
  echo "❌ Accessibility regression detected!"
  echo "Was: $BASELINE_VIOLATIONS, Now: $CURRENT_VIOLATIONS"
  exit 1
fi

docs.title: Multi-Page Testing
docs.text:
Test entire site:

#!/bin/bash
PAGES=(
  "/"
  "/about"
  "/products"
  "/contact"
  "/blog"
)

for page in "${PAGES[@]}"; do
  echo "Testing $page…"
  inspekt open "https://example.com$page" --wait
  inspekt axe --level 21aa --json > "audit-${page//\//-}.json"
done

# Summary report
echo "Page,Violations,Critical,Serious" > summary.csv
for file in audit-*.json; do
  PAGE=$(echo "$file" | sed 's/audit-//;s/.json//')
  TOTAL=$(jq '.summary.violationCount' "$file")
  CRITICAL=$(jq '.summary.criticalCount' "$file")
  SERIOUS=$(jq '.summary.seriousCount' "$file")
  echo "$PAGE,$TOTAL,$CRITICAL,$SERIOUS" >> summary.csv
done

cat summary.csv

docs.title: ✅ Do
docs.text:
• Test early and often during development
  • Fix critical and serious issues immediately
  • Test with real screen readers, not just automated tools
  • Test keyboard navigation manually
  • Include accessibility in code review
  • Document accessibility standards for your team
  • Test authenticated and dynamic states
  • Track accessibility metrics over time

docs.title: ❌ Don't
docs.text:
• Rely solely on automated testing (catches ~35% of issues)
  • Ignore "incomplete" checks (need manual review)
  • Use ARIA when semantic HTML suffices
  • Remove focus indicators (:focus outline)
  • Use color alone to convey information
  • Skip manual keyboard testing
  • Forget to test with zoom enabled
  • Assume your site is accessible without testing

docs.title: Accessible Name Computation
docs.text: Inspekt implements the W3C Accessible Name and Description Computation 1.2 (ACCNAME 1.2) specification for computing accessible names of elements during recording and replay.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text: When recording user interactions, Inspekt captures the accessible name of focused elements to provide meaningful feedback. This helps users understand which element is being interacted with, especially for elements that don't have visible text labels.

docs.title: ACCNAME 1.2 Compliance
docs.text: Our implementation follows the priority order defined in the ACCNAME 1.2 specification:

docs.title: 1. aria-labelledby (Highest Priority)
docs.text:
If an element has aria-labelledby, we recursively compute the accessible name from each referenced element.

<button aria-labelledby="label1 label2">...</button>
<span id="label1">Save</span>
<span id="label2">Document</span>
<!-- Accessible name: "Save Document" -->

docs.title: 2. aria-label
docs.text:
Direct aria-label attribute takes precedence over native HTML semantics.

<button aria-label="Close dialog">X</button>
<!-- Accessible name: "Close dialog" -->

docs.title: 3. Host Language Label (HTML Semantics)
docs.text:
For form controls, we check associated <label> elements:

<label for="email">Email address</label>
<input type="email" id="email">
<!-- Accessible name: "Email address" -->

docs.title: 4. Native Element Semantics
docs.text:
• img/area: alt attribute
  • input[type=image]: alt attribute
  • input[type=button/submit/reset]: value attribute
  • svg: <title> child element
<img src="logo.png" alt="Company Logo">
<!-- Accessible name: "Company Logo" -->

docs.title: 5. Name from Content
docs.text:
For elements with roles that support "name from content" (buttons, links, etc.), we recursively traverse child nodes:

<a href="/products">
  <img src="icon.svg" alt="View">
  Products
</a>
<!-- Accessible name: "View Products" -->

docs.title: 6. CSS Pseudo-elements
docs.text:
We include text content from ::before and ::after pseudo-elements:

<button class="icon-btn">Save</button>
<style>
  .icon-btn::before { content: "💾 "; }
</style>
<!-- Accessible name: "💾 Save" -->

docs.title: 7. Embedded Control Values
docs.text:
When computing name from content, embedded form controls contribute their current value:

<label>
  Volume: <input type="range" value="50"> %
</label>
<!-- Accessible name: "Volume: 50 %" -->

docs.title: 8. title Attribute (Fallback)
docs.text: The title attribute serves as a fallback when no other accessible name is available.

docs.title: 9. placeholder (Form Inputs Only)
docs.text: For input and textarea elements, the placeholder attribute is used as a last resort.

docs.title: Hidden Element Handling
docs.text:
Per ACCNAME 1.2, hidden elements do not contribute to accessible names unless explicitly referenced via aria-labelledby. We check for:

  • hidden HTML attribute
  • aria-hidden="true"
  • CSS display: none
  • CSS visibility: hidden

docs.title: Implementation Details
docs.text:
The accessible name computation is implemented in two JavaScript files:

  • inspekt/scripts/record_events.js - Used during recording
  • inspekt/scripts/replay_step.js - Used during replay

docs.title: Key Functions
docs.text: Function Purpose computeAccessibleName() Main entry point, implements priority cascade computeAccessibleNameFromContent() Recursive content traversal isEffectivelyHidden() CSS and ARIA hidden state detection getPseudoElementText() CSS pseudo-element content extraction

docs.title: Supported Features
docs.text: Feature Status aria-labelledby (recursive) ✅ Full support aria-label ✅ Full support Associated <label> elements ✅ Full support alt for img/area/input[type=image] ✅ Full support value for button inputs ✅ Full support SVG <title> element ✅ Full support Name from content ✅ Full support CSS pseudo-elements ✅ Full support Embedded control values ✅ Full support CSS hidden detection ✅ Full support title attribute fallback ✅ Full support placeholder fallback ✅ Full support

docs.title: Bash/Zsh Functions
docs.text:
Add these to your .bashrc or .zshrc:

# Quick page title
zt() {
  inspekt eval "document.title" --format raw
}

# Quick URL
zu() {
  inspekt eval "location.href" --format raw
}

# Extract all links
zlinks() {
  inspekt links --only-urls
}

# Count elements
zcount() {
  local selector="${1:-.item}"
  inspekt eval "document.querySelectorAll('$selector').length" --format raw
}

# Monitor element content
zwatch() {
  local selector="${1:-.main}"
  watch -n 5 "inspekt eval \"document.querySelector('$selector').textContent\" --format raw"
}

# Quick screenshot
zscreen() {
  local selector="${1:-body}"
  local output="screenshot-$(date +%Y%m%d-%H%M%S).png"
  inspekt screenshot --selector "$selector" --output "$output"
  echo "Saved: $output"
}

# ~/.bash_completion.d/inspekt

docs.title: Retry Logic
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

retry_command() {
  local max_attempts=3
  local attempt=1
  local delay=2

  while [ $attempt -le $max_attempts ]; do
    echo "Attempt $attempt/$max_attempts…"

    if "$@"; then
      return 0
    fi

    if [ $attempt -lt $max_attempts ]; then
      echo "Failed. Retrying in ${delay}s…"
      sleep $delay
      delay=$((delay * 2))
    fi

    attempt=$((attempt + 1))
  done

  echo "All attempts failed" >&2
  return 1
}

# Usage
retry_command inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.dynamic-content').textContent"

#!/bin/bash

# Extract data from multiple pages in parallel
urls=(
  "https://example.com/page1"
  "https://example.com/page2"
  "https://example.com/page3"
)

pids=()

for url in "${urls[@]}"; do
  (
    echo "Processing: $url"
    inspekt open "$url" --wait
    title=$(inspekt eval "document.title" --format raw)
    links=$(inspekt links --only-urls | wc -l)
    echo "$url,$title,$links" >> results.csv
  ) &
  pids+=($!)
done

# Wait for all to complete
for pid in "${pids[@]}"; do
  wait "$pid"
done

echo "All pages processed"

#!/bin/bash
# Scrape product data from multiple pages

output_file="products.jsonl"
base_url="https://example.com/products"
total_pages=5

> "$output_file"  # Clear file

for page in $(seq 1 $total_pages); do
  echo "Scraping page $page/$total_pages…"

  # Navigate
  inspekt open "${base_url}?page=${page}" --wait

  # Wait for products to load
  inspekt wait ".product" --visible

  # Extract data
  inspekt eval "
    Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.product')).map(p => ({
      name: p.querySelector('.product-name')?.textContent.trim(),
      price: p.querySelector('.product-price')?.textContent.trim(),
      rating: p.querySelector('.rating')?.textContent.trim(),
      image: p.querySelector('img')?.src,
      url: p.querySelector('a')?.href
    }))
  " --format json | jq -c '.[]' >> "$output_file"

  echo "Page $page complete"
  sleep 2  # Be polite
done

echo "Scraping complete. Total products: $(wc -l < "$output_file")"

#!/bin/bash
# Monitor page for changes and alert

url="https://example.com/status"
selector=".status-indicator"
check_interval=300  # 5 minutes
last_status=""

echo "Monitoring: $url"
echo "Selector: $selector"
echo "Interval: ${check_interval}s"

while true; do
  # Navigate and extract status
  inspekt open "$url" --wait
  current_status=$(inspekt eval "document.querySelector('$selector').textContent" --format raw)

  # Check for changes
  if [ -n "$last_status" ] && [ "$current_status" != "$last_status" ]; then
    echo "Status changed: $last_status → $current_status"

    # Send alert (macOS)
    osascript -e "display notification \"Status: $current_status\" with title \"Page Monitor\""

    # Or send email
    # echo "Status changed to: $current_status" | mail -s "Alert" user@example.com
  fi

  last_status="$current_status"
  echo "$(date): $current_status"

  sleep "$check_interval"
done

#!/bin/bash

echo "Running browser tests…"

# Start server if not running
if ! inspekt server status &>/dev/null; then
  inspekt server start --daemon
  sleep 2
  cleanup=true
fi

# Run tests
inspekt open "file://$(pwd)/tests/index.html" --wait

  if (typeof runTests !== 'function') {
    return {error: 'runTests not found'};
  }
  return runTests();
" --format json)

failed=$(echo "$result" | jq -r '.failed // 0')

# Cleanup if we started the server
if [ "$cleanup" = "true" ]; then

fi

# Check results

  echo "Tests failed! Commit aborted."
  echo "$result" | jq '.'
  exit 1
fi

echo "All tests passed!"

#!/bin/bash

cache_dir="$HOME/.inspekt-cache"
cache_ttl=300  # 5 minutes

mkdir -p "$cache_dir"

get_cached_or_fetch() {
  local key="$1"
  local command="$2"
  local cache_file="$cache_dir/$(echo "$key" | md5sum | cut -d' ' -f1)"

  # Check cache
  if [ -f "$cache_file" ]; then
    age=$(($(date +%s) - $(stat -c %Y "$cache_file")))
    if [ $age -lt $cache_ttl ]; then
      cat "$cache_file"
      return 0
    fi
  fi

  # Fetch and cache
  result=$(eval "$command")
  echo "$result" > "$cache_file"
  echo "$result"
}

# Usage
title=$(get_cached_or_fetch "page-title" "inspekt eval 'document.title' --format raw")

# Or use a secrets manager
# export INSPEKT_USERNAME=$(vault read -field=username secret/inspekt)
# export INSPEKT_PASSWORD=$(vault read -field=password secret/inspekt)

inspekt send "$INSPEKT_USERNAME" --selector "#username"
inspekt send "$INSPEKT_PASSWORD" --selector "#password"

docs.title: Avoid Logging Sensitive Data
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

# Good - don't log passwords
log_message "Logging in as $INSPEKT_USERNAME"

# Avoid
# log_message "Login: $INSPEKT_USERNAME / $INSPEKT_PASSWORD"

docs.title: Audit Logging
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash

log_file="$HOME/.inspekt-audit.log"

log_action() {
  echo "$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ) | $USER | $*" >> "$log_file"
}

# Log all commands
command="$*"
log_action "$command"
inspekt $command

docs.title: 1. Use Specific Selectors
docs.text:
# Good
inspekt click "#submit-btn"
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.product[data-id=\"123\"]')"

# Avoid
inspekt click "button"
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('div div div button')"

docs.title: 2. Handle Errors Gracefully
docs.text:
# Good
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.optional')?.textContent || 'Not found'"

# Avoid (may crash)
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.optional').textContent"

docs.title: 3. Batch Related Operations
docs.text:
# Good - single command
inspekt eval "({title: document.title, links: document.links.length})"

# Avoid - multiple commands
# inspekt eval "document.title"
# inspekt eval "document.links.length"

docs.title: 4. Use Appropriate Timeouts
docs.text:
# Quick operations
inspekt eval "document.title" --timeout 5

# Slow operations
inspekt eval "await fetch('/api/data').then(r => r.json())" --timeout 30

docs.title: 5. Test in Different Browsers
docs.text: Different browsers have different behaviors. Test your scripts in: - Chrome/Chromium - Firefox - Safari - Edge

docs.title: Command Hangs
docs.text:

inspekt eval "document.title" --timeout 5

# Check for infinite loops
inspekt eval "console.log('test'); document.title"

docs.title: High Memory Usage
docs.text:

# Clear caches periodically
rm -rf "$HOME/.inspekt-cache"/*

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
# Add delays between requests
for url in "${urls[@]}"; do
  inspekt open "$url" --wait
  inspekt eval "document.title"
  sleep 2  # Be polite
done

docs.title: AI Features
docs.text: Master AI-powered features in Inspekt. Learn how to generate article summaries, create page descriptions for accessibility, and configure AI integration with mods.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Inspekt integrates with AI through mods to provide two powerful features:

  • inspekt summarize - Generate concise article summaries
  • inspekt describe - Create accessible page descriptions for screen readers

Both commands extract page content and use AI to generate natural-language output.

docs.title: Install mods
docs.text:
AI features require mods to be installed:

# macOS/Linux
brew install charmbracelet/tap/mods

# Or with go
go install github.com/charmbracelet/mods@latest

docs.title: Configure mods
docs.text:
On first run, mods will prompt you to configure an AI provider:

mods

Supported providers: - OpenAI (GPT-3.5, GPT-4) - Anthropic (Claude) - Ollama (local models) - Azure OpenAI - And more...

Set your API key:

# OpenAI
export OPENAI_API_KEY="your-key-here"

# Anthropic
export ANTHROPIC_API_KEY="your-key-here"

# Or configure via mods
mods --settings

docs.title: Article Summarization
docs.text: The inspekt summarize command extracts article content and generates a concise summary.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
inspekt summarize

Example output: 

This article discusses the importance of web accessibility and provides
practical techniques for making websites more inclusive. Key points include
semantic HTML, ARIA labels, keyboard navigation, and screen reader compatibility.
The author emphasizes that accessibility benefits all users, not just those with
disabilities, by improving usability and SEO.

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
1. Extract Article - Uses Mozilla Readability to extract main content
  2. Detect Language - Automatically detects page language
  3. Generate Summary - Sends content to AI via mods
  4. Return Result - Displays concise summary

docs.title: Show Full Article
docs.text:
inspekt summarize --format full

Displays the extracted article content without summarizing:

Title: Web Accessibility Best Practices
Author: John Doe
Published: 2024-01-15

Web accessibility is crucial for creating inclusive digital experiences...
[Full extracted article text]

docs.title: Language Control
docs.text:
Override the output language:

# Summarize in French
inspekt summarize --language fr
inspekt summarize --lang fr

# Summarize in Spanish
inspekt summarize --language es

# Summarize in German
inspekt summarize --lang de

docs.title: Language Detection Flow
docs.text:
1. CLI flag (--language) - Highest priority
  2. Config file (ai-language setting) - Second priority
  3. Page language (HTML lang attribute) - Third priority
  4. Let AI decide - Default behavior

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
See the full prompt sent to AI:

inspekt summarize --debug

Output: 

=== PROMPT ===
Please summarize the following article in 2-3 sentences.
Respond in English.

Title: Web Accessibility Best Practices
Content: [article content]
=== END PROMPT ===

Useful for: - Understanding what's sent to AI - Debugging language issues - Customizing prompts

docs.title: Custom Prompts
docs.text:
Edit the summarization prompt:

# Edit prompt file
nano ~/inspekt_bridge/prompts/summary.prompt

Default prompt: 

Please summarize the following article in 2-3 concise sentences.
Focus on the main points and key takeaways.

{LANGUAGE_INSTRUCTION}

Title: {TITLE}
Content: {CONTENT}

Variables: - {LANGUAGE_INSTRUCTION} - Injected when --language is used - {TITLE} - Article title - {CONTENT} - Extracted article text

docs.title: Page Descriptions for Screen Readers
docs.text: The inspekt describe command generates natural-language page descriptions perfect for blind users.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
inspekt describe

Example output: 

This webpage is in Dutch, but is also available in English and French.
At the top you can navigate to services, articles, careers, about us
and contact us. The main part contains a rather long article about an
empathy lab with five headings. The footer contains standard links
such as a sitemap and privacy statement.

docs.title: What It Analyzes
docs.text:
The describe command extracts:

  • Available languages - Alternate language versions
  • Navigation menus - Main navigation structure
  • Page landmarks - Headers, main content, footer, etc.
  • Heading structure - H1-H6 hierarchy and count
  • Main content type - Article, form, list, etc.
  • Content length - Approximate reading time
  • Significant images - Alt text and image count
  • Forms - Input fields and their purposes
  • Footer utilities - Links like privacy policy, sitemap

docs.title: Language Control
docs.text:
# Describe in French
inspekt describe --language fr

# Describe in Spanish
inspekt describe --lang es

docs.title: Debug Mode
docs.text:
inspekt describe --debug

See the extracted page structure and full prompt.

docs.title: Custom Prompts
docs.text:
Edit the description prompt:

nano ~/inspekt_bridge/prompts/describe.prompt

Default prompt: 

Create a concise description of this webpage for a blind user using a screen reader.
Focus on:
- Available languages
- Navigation structure
- Main content type and purpose
- Interactive elements
- Overall page organization

Keep it natural and conversational.

{LANGUAGE_INSTRUCTION}

Page Structure:
{PAGE_STRUCTURE}

docs.title: Language Settings
docs.text:
Set default AI output language in config.json:

{
  "ai-language": "en"
}

Supported languages: - en - English - es - Spanish - fr - French - de - German - nl - Dutch - it - Italian - pt - Portuguese - ja - Japanese - zh - Chinese - And more...

Configure mods behavior:

mods --settings

# Use specific model
mods --model gpt-4

# Use local model with Ollama
mods --model ollama:llama2

inspekt summarize

inspekt summarize > summary1.txt
# Navigate to another article

docs.title: Content Curation
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Batch summarize articles

URLS=(
  "https://example.com/article1"
  "https://example.com/article2"
  "https://example.com/article3"
)

for url in "${URLS[@]}"; do
  echo "=== $url ===" >> summaries.txt
  inspekt open "$url" --wait
  inspekt summarize >> summaries.txt
  echo "" >> summaries.txt
done

docs.text:

docs.title: Multilingual Research Workflow
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Research workflow with translations

# Navigate to French article
inspekt open "https://example.fr/article"

# Get English summary
inspekt summarize --language en > summary-en.txt

# Get French summary

docs.title: Accessibility Audit
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Audit multiple pages

PAGES=(
  "https://example.com/"
  "https://example.com/about"
  "https://example.com/contact"
)

for page in "${PAGES[@]}"; do
  echo "Auditing: $page"
  inspekt open "$page" --wait

  # Get description
  echo "Description:" >> audit.txt
  inspekt describe >> audit.txt

  # Get outline
  echo "Outline:" >> audit.txt
  inspekt outline >> audit.txt

  # Get link analysis
  echo "Links:" >> audit.txt
  inspekt links --only-internal >> audit.txt

  echo "---" >> audit.txt
done

docs.title: Content Monitoring
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Monitor article changes

URL="https://example.com/article"

while true; do
  inspekt open "$URL" --wait
  SUMMARY=$(inspekt summarize)

  if [[ "$SUMMARY" != "$LAST_SUMMARY" ]]; then
    echo "Article updated: $URL"
    echo "$SUMMARY"
    LAST_SUMMARY="$SUMMARY"
  fi

  sleep 3600  # Check every hour
done

docs.title: No Article Content Found
docs.text:
Error: 

Error: Could not extract article content

Possible causes: - Page is not an article (try a blog post or news article) - Content is behind login - Page uses non-standard structure

Solution: Use inspekt eval to extract manually: 

inspekt eval "document.querySelector('article')?.textContent"

docs.title: Rate Limiting
docs.text:
Error: 

Error: Rate limit exceeded

Solution: - Wait and retry - Use a different AI provider - Use local models with Ollama

docs.title: Token Usage
docs.text:
AI features consume tokens:

Typical usage: - inspekt summarize - 500-2000 tokens (depending on article length) - inspekt describe - 300-800 tokens (depending on page complexity)

Cost estimates (OpenAI GPT-3.5-Turbo): - ~\(0.001 per summary - ~\)0.0005 per description

Cost estimates (Claude Sonnet): - ~\(0.003 per summary - ~\)0.001 per description

docs.title: Optimization Tips
docs.text:
1. Use cheaper models for simple tasks
  2. Batch operations instead of repeated calls
  3. Use local models (Ollama) for free inference
  4. Cache results for frequently accessed pages

ollama pull llama2

# Use normally
inspekt summarize
inspekt describe

Always review AI-generated content:

inspekt summarize --format full

docs.text:
Match output language to use case:

# Native language for accessibility
inspekt describe --language fr  # For French site

Tailor prompts to your needs:

Track API usage:

docs.title: Basic Commands
docs.text: Learn the essential commands for everyday use with Inspekt. This guide covers the most common commands you'll use for executing code, getting page information, managing the server, and working interactively.

docs.title: Server Management
docs.text: Before you can use any commands, the bridge server must be running.

docs.title: Starting the Server
docs.text:
Start All Servers (Recommended)Start Bridge OnlyForeground ModeCustom Ports 
inspekt start

Starts both the bridge server and API server in daemon mode (background). Servers keep running even if you close your terminal.

inspekt start --bridge-only

Start only the bridge server. Useful if you don't need the HTTP API.

inspekt start --bridge-only --foreground

Starts the server in foreground mode. Useful for debugging. Press Ctrl+C to stop.

inspekt start --bridge-port 9000 --api-port 3000

Start on different ports (defaults: bridge=8765, API=8000).

Auto-start on Login

On macOS/Linux, you can create a launch agent or systemd service to start the servers automatically when you log in.

docs.title: Checking Server Status
docs.text:
inspekt status

Example output: 

Inspekt Server Status

============================================================
BRIDGE SERVER
============================================================

Server Information:
  Version:           1.0.0
  Uptime:            2h 15m 30s
  HTTP API:          http://127.0.0.1:8765
  WebSocket:         ws://127.0.0.1:8766

Connected Browser Instances:
  Total:             1 active connection

Request Statistics:
  Pending:           0
  Total Processed:   42 (since startup)
  Succeeded:         42
  Failed:            0

============================================================
API SERVER
============================================================

✓ Running
  Port:              8000
  URL:               http://localhost:8000

Shows comprehensive information including: - Server version and uptime - Connected browsers - Request statistics - API server status

docs.title: Stopping the Server
docs.text:
inspekt stop

Stops both bridge and API servers running in daemon mode.

Stop All ServersStop Only API ServerStop Only Bridge Server 
inspekt stop

inspekt stop --api-only

inspekt stop --bridge-only

Foreground Mode

If running servers in foreground mode, press Ctrl+C to stop them.

docs.title: Restarting the Server
docs.text:
inspekt restart

Stops and restarts both servers. Useful after configuration changes or when applying updates.

docs.title: Request Queue Management
docs.text: The bridge server maintains a queue of pending requests. If requests get stuck (e.g., browser disconnects before responding), you can inspect and clear the queue.

docs.title: Checking Queue Status
docs.text:
inspekt queue status

Example output: 

Queue Status

  Pending requests:   3
  Completed (cached): 12

Pending Requests:
  ID         Age        Type
  a1b2c3d4   45.2s      execute
  e5f6g7h8   32.1s      execute
  i9j0k1l2   12.8s      execute

⚠️  3 request(s) pending for >10 seconds

Shows: - Number of pending and completed requests - Details of each pending request (ID, age, type) - Warning if requests are stuck for too long

docs.title: Clearing Stuck Requests
docs.text:
# Clear all pending requests
inspekt queue clear

# Clear only requests older than 30 seconds
inspekt queue clear --older-than 30

# Skip confirmation prompt
inspekt queue clear --force

Example output: 

✓ Cleared 3 pending request(s)
  Remaining: 0

docs.title: Automatic Cleanup
docs.text:
The bridge server includes automatic cleanup:

  • Background watchdog - Runs every 30 seconds, removes stale requests
  • Warning logs - Alerts when requests are stuck for >60 seconds
  • Auto-expiration - Requests older than 2 minutes are automatically removed

When to Clear the Queue

Use inspekt queue clear if you see repeated timeouts or if inspekt status shows many pending requests. This is faster than restarting the server.

docs.title: Executing JavaScript Code
docs.text: The inspekt eval command is your primary way to execute JavaScript in the browser.

docs.title: Basic Syntax
docs.text: inspekt eval "javascript_code_here"

docs.title: Simple Expressions
docs.text:
Get quick information from the page:

# Page title
inspekt eval "document.title"
# Output: Example Domain

# Page URL
inspekt eval "location.href"
# Output: https://example.com/

# Number of links
inspekt eval "document.links.length"
# Output: 15

# Get domain
inspekt eval "location.hostname"
# Output: example.com

docs.title: Complex Expressions
docs.text:
Use arrays, objects, and methods:

# Extract all links
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.links).map(a => a.href)"

# Get multiple properties
inspekt eval "({url: location.href, title: document.title, links: document.links.length})"

# Filter elements
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a')).filter(a => a.hostname !== location.hostname).map(a => a.href)"

docs.title: Multi-line Code
docs.text:
For complex logic, use proper JavaScript syntax:

inspekt eval "
  const links = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a'));
  const internal = links.filter(a => a.hostname === location.hostname);
  const external = links.filter(a => a.hostname !== location.hostname);
  return {
    total: links.length,
    internal: internal.length,
    external: external.length
  };
"

Semicolons Matter

When using multiple statements, separate them with semicolons. The last expression is automatically returned.

docs.title: Using stdin
docs.text:
Pipe JavaScript code from files or other commands:

# From a file
cat script.js | inspekt eval

# From echo
echo "document.title" | inspekt eval

# From heredoc
inspekt eval <<'EOF'
const images = document.querySelectorAll('img');
return Array.from(images).map(img => ({
  src: img.src,
  alt: img.alt,
  width: img.naturalWidth,
  height: img.naturalHeight
}));
EOF

docs.title: Executing Files
docs.text: The inspekt exec command executes JavaScript from a file.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
inspekt exec script.js

Same as: 

inspekt eval --file script.js

docs.title: Example Script
docs.text:
script.js: 

// Extract all product information
const products = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.product'));
return products.map(product => ({
  name: product.querySelector('.product-name').textContent,
  price: product.querySelector('.product-price').textContent,
  rating: product.querySelector('.product-rating')?.textContent,
  image: product.querySelector('.product-image')?.src
}));

Execute: 

inspekt exec script.js --format json > products.json

docs.title: Built-in Scripts
docs.text:
Inspekt includes ready-to-use scripts:

# Extract all images with metadata
inspekt exec inspekt/scripts/extract_images.js --format json

# Extract table data
inspekt exec inspekt/scripts/extract_table.js --format json

# Get SEO metadata
inspekt exec inspekt/scripts/extract_metadata.js --format json

# Performance metrics
inspekt exec inspekt/scripts/performance_metrics.js --format json

# Inject jQuery
inspekt exec inspekt/scripts/inject_jquery.js

docs.title: Page Information
docs.text: Get comprehensive information about the current page.

docs.title: Basic Info
docs.text:
inspekt info

Output: 

URL:      https://example.com
Title:    Example Domain
Domain:   example.com
Protocol: https:
State:    complete
Size:     1280x720

Shows: - Current URL - Page title - Domain name - Protocol (http/https) - Document ready state - Window dimensions

docs.title: Extended Information
docs.text:
inspekt info --extended

Includes additional details: - Language & Encoding - Page language, character set - Meta Tags - Description, keywords, viewport - Resources - Script count, stylesheet count, cookie count - Security - HTTPS, mixed content warnings, CSP headers - Accessibility - Landmark count, heading structure, alt text issues - SEO - Canonical URL, Open Graph tags, structured data - Storage - localStorage and sessionStorage sizes - Service Workers - Registration status

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
inspekt info --json

Outputs all information as JSON for parsing with jq or other tools:

inspekt info --json | jq '.url'
inspekt info --json | jq '.title'

docs.title: Interactive REPL
docs.text: Start a live JavaScript session to experiment interactively.

docs.title: Starting the REPL
docs.text:
inspekt repl

Output: 

Connected to: Example Domain
https://example.com

Type 'exit' or press Ctrl+D to quit.

inspekt>

docs.title: Using the REPL
docs.text:
Type JavaScript code and press Enter:

inspekt> document.title
"Example Domain"

inspekt> document.querySelectorAll('p').length
2

inspekt> const links = Array.from(document.links)
undefined

inspekt> links.length
10

inspekt> links.map(a => a.href)
[
  "https://example.com/page1",
  "https://example.com/page2",
  ...
]

inspekt> exit
Goodbye!

docs.title: REPL Features
docs.text:
• State preservation - Variables persist across commands
  • Multi-line editing - Use arrow keys to edit history
  • Auto-display - Last expression is automatically printed
  • Error messages - Syntax and runtime errors are shown clearly

REPL Shortcuts

  • Ctrl+D or exit - Quit REPL
  • Ctrl+C - Cancel current line
  • Up/Down arrows - Navigate history

docs.title: REPL Use Cases
docs.text:
Testing selectors: 

inspekt> document.querySelector('.main-content')
[object HTMLDivElement]

inspekt> $0.textContent  // if using DevTools
"Main content here…"

Experimenting with APIs: 

inspekt> await fetch('/api/data').then(r => r.json())
{userId: 1, name: "John Doe"}

Debugging: 

inspekt> window.myApp
{state: {...}, config: {...}}

inspekt> window.myApp.state
{user: {...}, settings: {...}}

docs.title: Output Formatting
docs.text: Control how results are displayed using the --format flag.

docs.title: Format Options
docs.text: Format Description Best For auto (default) Smart formatting based on output type General use json Valid JSON output Piping to jq, scripts raw Plain text, no formatting Shell variables, parsing

docs.title: Auto Format (Default)
docs.text:
inspekt eval "document.title"

Intelligently formats based on the result type: - Strings: plain text - Objects/Arrays: pretty-printed JSON - Numbers: plain text - undefined/null: "(empty)"

docs.title: JSON Format
docs.text:
inspekt eval "({title: document.title, url: location.href})" --format json

Output: 

{
  "title": "Example Domain",
  "url": "https://example.com"
}

Perfect for piping to jq: 

inspekt eval "({title: document.title, url: location.href})" --format json | jq '.title'

docs.title: Raw Format
docs.text:
inspekt eval "document.title" --format raw

Output: 

Example Domain

No extra formatting - perfect for shell variables: 

TITLE=$(inspekt eval "document.title" --format raw)
echo "Page title is: $TITLE"

docs.title: Adding Metadata
docs.text:
Add URL and title to output:

# Add URL
inspekt eval "document.links.length" --url

# Add title
inspekt eval "document.links.length" --title

# Add both
inspekt eval "document.links.length" --url --title

Output: 

URL: https://example.com
Title: Example Domain

15

docs.title: Timeout Control
docs.text:
Commands have a default 10-second timeout. Adjust for slow operations.

# Default timeout (10 seconds)
inspekt eval "document.title"

# Custom timeout (30 seconds)
inspekt eval "await slowOperation()" --timeout 30

# Short timeout (5 seconds)
inspekt eval "document.title" --timeout 5

Timeouts

If a command takes longer than the timeout, you'll see: 

Error: Request timed out after 10 seconds

Increase the timeout with --timeout.

docs.title: Userscript Information
docs.text:
View installation instructions for the browser userscript.

inspekt userscript

Displays: - Installation instructions - Userscript manager links (Violentmonkey, Tampermonkey) - How to view the userscript code

docs.text:
# Title
inspekt eval "document.title"

# URL
inspekt eval "location.href"

# Domain
inspekt eval "location.hostname"

# Full page info
inspekt info

docs.title: Count Elements
docs.text:
# All links
inspekt eval "document.links.length"

# All images
inspekt eval "document.images.length"

# Specific selector
inspekt eval "document.querySelectorAll('.product').length"

docs.title: Extract Text
docs.text:
# Page text
inspekt eval "document.body.textContent"

# Heading text
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('h1').textContent"

# All headings
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('h1,h2,h3')).map(h => h.textContent)"

docs.title: Check Existence
docs.text:
# Element exists
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.modal') !== null"

# Element visible
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.modal')?.offsetParent !== null"

docs.title: Common Errors
docs.text:
Server not running: 

Error: Bridge server is not running
Please start the server with: inspekt start

Solution: Start the server with inspekt start

No browser connection: 

Error: No response from browser

Solutions: - Ensure the userscript is installed and enabled - Open a browser tab (userscript only works in active tabs) - Check browser console for errors - Refresh the page

Timeout: 

Error: Request timed out after 10 seconds

Solution: Increase timeout with --timeout 30

JavaScript error: 

TypeError: Cannot read property 'click' of null

Solution: Check your selectors - element may not exist

docs.title: Use Shell Variables
docs.text:
TITLE=$(inspekt eval "document.title" --format raw)
URL=$(inspekt eval "location.href" --format raw)

echo "Title: $TITLE"
echo "URL: $URL"

docs.title: Pipe to Other Tools
docs.text:
# Count links
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.links).map(a => a.href).join('\n')" --format raw | wc -l

# Filter with grep
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.links).map(a => a.href).join('\n')" --format raw | grep "github"

# Process with jq
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.links).map(a => ({text: a.textContent, href: a.href}))" --format json | jq '.[0]'

docs.title: Async/Await Support
docs.text: inspekt eval "await fetch('/api/data').then(r => r.json())"

docs.title: Console Logging
docs.text:
inspekt eval "console.log('Debug info'); document.title"

Check your browser console to see the log output.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• JavaScript Execution - Deep dive into code execution
  • Element Interaction - Click, inspect, and interact with elements
  • Data Extraction - Extract structured data from pages

docs.title: Quick Reference
docs.text:
Command Purpose Example inspekt start Start servers in background inspekt start --bridge-only inspekt stop Stop servers inspekt stop --api-only inspekt restart Restart servers inspekt restart inspekt status Check server status - inspekt queue status Check request queue - inspekt queue clear Clear stuck requests inspekt queue clear --older-than 30 inspekt eval "code" Execute JavaScript inspekt eval "document.title" inspekt exec file.js Execute file inspekt exec script.js inspekt info Get page info inspekt info --extended inspekt repl Interactive mode - inspekt userscript View userscript info -

You're Ready!

You now know the essential commands to control your browser from the terminal. Explore the other guides to learn advanced features!

docs.title: CLI vs HTTP API: Which Should You Use?
docs.text:
Inspekt provides two interfaces to control your browser: a Command-Line Interface (CLI) and an HTTP API. Both use the same underlying code, but they're optimized for different use cases.

This guide will help you understand when to use each one.

docs.title: Quick Decision Guide
docs.text:
graph TD
    A[What do you need?] --> B{Interactive<br/>terminal work?}
    B -->|Yes| C[Use CLI]
    B -->|No| D{Making many<br/>requests?}
    D -->|Yes| E[Use API]
    D -->|No| F{Integration with<br/>other tools?}
    F -->|Yes| E
    F -->|No| G{Need formatted<br/>human output?}
    G -->|Yes| C
    G -->|No| E

docs.title: At a Glance Comparison
docs.text: Feature CLI HTTP API Speed (per request) ~430ms ~60ms (7x faster) Startup time Every command Once (stays running) Output format Human-friendly JSON (machine-readable) Best for Interactive use Automation & integration Learning curve Easier Moderate Features Full (colors, prompts) Core functionality Integration Shell scripts Any language/tool

docs.title: The Numbers
docs.text:
Let's look at actual performance measurements:

# Single CLI command
time inspekt info
# Real time: ~430ms

# Single API request
time curl http://localhost:8767/api/extraction/info
# Real time: ~60ms

# 10 CLI commands
time for i in {1..10}; do inspekt info > /dev/null; done
# Real time: ~4.3 seconds (430ms each)

# 10 API requests
time for i in {1..10}; do curl -s http://localhost:8767/api/extraction/info > /dev/null; done
# Real time: ~0.6 seconds (60ms each)

The API is ~7x faster for repeated requests!

docs.title: CLI Overhead
docs.text:
When you run a CLI command, here's what happens:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. Start Python interpreter         ~200ms │
│ 2. Import all modules                ~100ms │
│ 3. Parse command-line arguments       ~50ms │
│ 4. Check userscript version          ~100ms │ ⚠️
│ 5. Execute JavaScript in browser      ~50ms │
│ 6. Format output for terminal         ~20ms │
│ 7. Print with colors/formatting       ~10ms │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Total:                               ~530ms │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Key points: - Python starts fresh every time - Version check makes an extra HTTP request - Formatting adds overhead - But you get nice, human-readable output!

docs.title: API Speed
docs.text:
When you call the API:

┌─────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│ 1. HTTP request to running server     ~5ms │
│ 2. FastAPI validates request           ~2ms │
│ 3. Execute JavaScript in browser      ~50ms │
│ 4. Return raw JSON                     ~3ms │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ Total:                                ~60ms │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────┘

Key points: - Server is already running (no startup) - No version check on every request - Minimal formatting overhead - Returns raw JSON immediately

docs.title: Visualizing the Difference
docs.text:
Here's a visual representation of 10 requests:

CLI (10 requests = 4.3 seconds): 

Request 1: [■■■■■■■■■] 430ms
Request 2: [■■■■■■■■■] 430ms
Request 3: [■■■■■■■■■] 430ms

Request 9: [■■■■■■■■■] 430ms
Request 10:[■■■■■■■■■] 430ms

API (10 requests = 0.6 seconds): 

Request 1: [■] 60ms
Request 2: [■] 60ms
Request 3: [■] 60ms
Request 4: [■] 60ms
Request 5: [■] 60ms
Request 6: [■] 60ms
Request 7: [■] 60ms
