Request 10:[■] 60ms

docs.title: 1. Interactive Terminal Work
docs.text:
When you're exploring a website manually:

# Open a page
inspekt open "https://example.com"

# Look at the page structure
inspekt outline

# Extract some data
inspekt links

# Get page info
inspekt info

Why CLI is better: Nice formatted output, colors, easy to read.

docs.title: 2. One-Off Commands
docs.text:
Quick tasks you run occasionally:

# Take a screenshot
inspekt screenshot output.png

# Get a page summary
inspekt summarize

# Execute some JavaScript
inspekt eval "document.title"

Why CLI is better: No need to start a server, just run and done.

docs.title: 3. Shell Scripts
docs.text:
Simple automation in bash/zsh scripts:

#!/bin/bash
# check-website.sh

inspekt open "https://mysite.com"
sleep 2

if inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.error')" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    echo "❌ Error found on page"
    exit 1
else
    echo "✅ Page looks good"
fi

Why CLI is better: Integrates naturally with shell scripts, exit codes work well.

docs.title: 4. Human-Readable Output
docs.text:
When you need output formatted for humans:

inspekt info

URL:      https://example.com
Title:    Example Domain
Domain:   example.com
Protocol: https:
State:    complete
Size:     1280x720

Inspekt: Extension v4.2.1

Why CLI is better: Output is formatted, colored, and easy to scan visually.

docs.title: 5. Interactive Features
docs.text:
Commands that need user interaction:

# Control browser with keyboard
inspekt control

# Interactive REPL
inspekt repl

# Download with interactive selection
inspekt download

Why CLI is better: These features require terminal interaction, prompts, keyboard input.

docs.title: ❌ Not Ideal For:
docs.text:
• High-frequency requests (>10 per minute)
  • Integration with web applications
  • When you need raw JSON data
  • Performance-critical automation
  • Non-Python environments

docs.title: When to Use the HTTP API
1. High-Frequency Automation
docs.text:
When making many requests in succession:

import requests

session = requests.Session()
API = "http://localhost:8767"

# Fast: Reuses connection
for url in urls:
    session.post(f"{API}/api/navigation/open", json={"url": url})
    info = session.get(f"{API}/api/extraction/info").json()

    if "error" in info["result"]["title"]:
        alert_team(url)

Why API is better: 7x faster, reuses HTTP connection, no startup overhead.

docs.title: 2. Web Application Integration
docs.text:
Building a web dashboard or service:

// Frontend JavaScript
async function getPageInfo() {
    const response = await fetch('http://localhost:8767/api/extraction/info');
    const data = await response.json();

    document.getElementById('title').textContent = data.result.title;
    document.getElementById('url').textContent = data.result.url;
}

// Update every 2 seconds
setInterval(getPageInfo, 2000);

Why API is better: Native JSON, works from browser, modern web apps expect REST APIs.

docs.title: 3. Microservice Architecture
docs.text:
Part of a larger system:

# docker-compose.yml
services:
  inspekt-api:
    image: inspekt-bridge-api
    ports:
      - "8767:8767"

  monitor-service:
    image: website-monitor
    environment:
      - INSPEKT_API=http://inspekt-api:8767

Why API is better: Containers, service discovery, standard HTTP protocols.

docs.title: 4. Cross-Language Integration
docs.text:
Using Inspekt from non-Python languages:

// Node.js
const axios = require('axios');

async function checkPage(url) {
    await axios.post('http://localhost:8767/api/navigation/open', {
        url: url,
        wait: true
    });

    const info = await axios.get('http://localhost:8767/api/extraction/info');
    return info.data;
}

# Ruby
require 'httparty'

response = HTTParty.post('http://localhost:8767/api/navigation/open',
    body: { url: 'https://example.com', wait: true }.to_json,
    headers: { 'Content-Type' => 'application/json' }
)

// Go
package main

import (
    "bytes"
    "encoding/json"
    "net/http"
)

func navigate(url string) error {
    body, _ := json.Marshal(map[string]interface{}{
        "url": url,
        "wait": true,
    })

    _, err := http.Post(
        "http://localhost:8767/api/navigation/open",
        "application/json",
        bytes.NewBuffer(body),
    )
    return err
}

Why API is better: HTTP is universal, every language has HTTP clients.

docs.title: 5. Monitoring & Alerting
docs.text:
Continuous monitoring systems:

import requests
import time

API = "http://localhost:8767"

while True:
    # Navigate to page
    requests.post(f"{API}/api/navigation/open",
                  json={"url": "https://mysite.com"})

    # Check for errors
    result = requests.post(f"{API}/api/execution/eval",
                          json={"code": "document.querySelector('.error') !== null"})

    if result.json()["result"]:
        send_alert("Error detected on website!")

    time.sleep(60)  # Check every minute

Why API is better: Long-running process, efficient, can run 24/7.

docs.title: 6. Machine-Readable Data
docs.text:
When you need JSON for processing:

# API returns clean JSON
curl http://localhost:8767/api/extraction/links | jq '.result[] | .href'

{
  "ok": true,
  "result": [
    {"href": "https://example.com/1", "text": "Link 1"},
    {"href": "https://example.com/2", "text": "Link 2"}
  ]
}

Why API is better: JSON is easy to parse, process with jq, store in databases.

docs.title: ❌ Not Ideal For:
docs.text:
• Quick one-off tasks
  • When you want human-readable output
  • Interactive terminal features
  • Learning Inspekt (CLI is more intuitive)

docs.title: Hybrid Approaches
docs.text: You don't have to choose just one! Here are patterns that use both:

docs.title: Pattern 1: Development with CLI, Production with API
docs.text:
# During development - use CLI for exploration
inspekt open "https://example.com"
inspekt outline
inspekt info

# Once you know what you need, automate with API
curl http://localhost:8767/api/extraction/info > data.json

docs.title: Pattern 2: Shell Scripts with API for Performance
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# monitor.sh - Uses API for speed

API="http://localhost:8767"

# Fast: API calls
for url in $(cat urls.txt); do
    curl -s -X POST "$API/api/navigation/open" \
        -H "Content-Type: application/json" \
        -d "{\"url\":\"$url\"}"

    info=$(curl -s "$API/api/extraction/info")
    title=$(echo "$info" | jq -r '.result.title')
    echo "Checked: $title"
done

# Nice output: CLI for final report
echo "\nFull report:"
inspekt info --extended

docs.title: Pattern 3: CLI for Setup, API for Execution
docs.text:
# Use CLI to start servers
inspekt server start
uvicorn inspekt.app.api.server:app --host 127.0.0.1 --port 8767 &

# Use API for the heavy lifting
python automation_script.py  # Uses HTTP API

# Use CLI for final checks
inspekt info
inspekt screenshot final-state.png

docs.title: For CLI Users
docs.text:
If you need better CLI performance:

  1. Use --json flag for faster output: 

    inspekt info --json | jq

  2. Batch commands in shell scripts: 

    # Slower: Multiple commands
inspekt eval "document.title"
inspekt eval "document.URL"

# Faster: One command
inspekt eval "({title: document.title, url: document.URL})" --format json

  3. Keep bridge server running: 

    inspekt server start --daemon  # Only start once

docs.title: For API Users
docs.text:
To maximize API performance:

  1. Reuse HTTP connections: 

    session = requests.Session()  # Reuse connection
for _ in range(100):
    session.get("http://localhost:8767/api/extraction/info")

  2. Use connection pooling: 

    from requests.adapters import HTTPAdapter
from urllib3.util.retry import Retry

session = requests.Session()
adapter = HTTPAdapter(pool_connections=10, pool_maxsize=20)
session.mount('http://', adapter)

  3. Batch requests when possible: 

    # Instead of many small requests
results = []
for url in urls:
    # ... multiple API calls per URL

# Better: Collect data, process in bulk
data = session.get(f"{API}/api/extraction/info").json()
process_batch(data)

docs.title: Example 1: Daily Website Check (Use CLI)
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# daily-check.sh - Run once per day

inspekt open "https://mysite.com"
sleep 3

# Get summary
inspekt describe > summary.txt

# Take screenshot
inspekt screenshot website-$(date +%Y%m%d).png

# Email report
mail -s "Daily Website Check" admin@example.com < summary.txt

Why CLI: Runs once daily, human-readable output, simple script.

docs.title: Example 2: Real-Time Monitoring (Use API)
docs.text:
# monitor.py - Runs continuously

import requests
import time
from datetime import datetime

API = "http://localhost:8767"
session = requests.Session()

while True:
    # Navigate
    session.post(f"{API}/api/navigation/open",
                 json={"url": "https://mysite.com", "wait": True})

    # Extract data
    info = session.get(f"{API}/api/extraction/info").json()

    # Log to database
    log_to_database({
        "timestamp": datetime.now(),
        "title": info["result"]["title"],
        "status": "ok" if info["ok"] else "error"
    })

    time.sleep(30)  # Check every 30 seconds

Why API: Continuous running, efficient, structured data.

docs.title: Example 3: Web Dashboard (Use API)
docs.text:
<!DOCTYPE html>
<html>
<head>
    <title>Browser Monitor</title>
</head>
<body>
    <h1>Current Page: <span id="title"></span></h1>
    <p>URL: <span id="url"></span></p>
    <button onclick="refresh()">Refresh</button>

    <script>
    async function refresh() {
        const response = await fetch('http://localhost:8767/api/extraction/info');
        const data = await response.json();

        document.getElementById('title').textContent = data.result.title;
        document.getElementById('url').textContent = data.result.url;
    }

    // Auto-refresh every 5 seconds
    setInterval(refresh, 5000);
    refresh();
    </script>
</body>
</html>

Why API: Web integration, real-time updates, works in browser.

docs.title: Example 4: Data Collection Script (Use API)
docs.text:
# collect-data.py - Efficient data collection

import requests
import csv

API = "http://localhost:8767"
session = requests.Session()

urls = ["https://site1.com", "https://site2.com", "https://site3.com"]
results = []

for url in urls:
    # Navigate
    session.post(f"{API}/api/navigation/open", json={"url": url, "wait": True})

    # Get info
    info = session.get(f"{API}/api/extraction/info").json()

    # Extract links
    links = session.get(f"{API}/api/extraction/links").json()

    results.append({
        "url": url,
        "title": info["result"]["title"],
        "link_count": len(links["result"])
    })

# Save to CSV
with open('results.csv', 'w') as f:
    writer = csv.DictWriter(f, fieldnames=['url', 'title', 'link_count'])
    writer.writeheader()
    writer.writerows(results)

Why API: Many requests, structured data, CSV export.

docs.title: Use the CLI when you want:
docs.text:
• 🖥️ Interactive terminal work
  • 👤 Human-readable output
  • 🎨 Colors and formatting
  • 🔧 Simple shell scripts
  • 📖 Easy learning curve
  • ⚡ Quick one-off commands

docs.title: Use the HTTP API when you need:
docs.text:
• ⚡ High performance (7x faster)
  • 🔄 Many repeated requests
  • 🌐 Integration with web apps
  • 🤖 Machine-readable JSON
  • 🔌 Cross-language support
  • 📊 Continuous monitoring
  • 🏗️ Microservices architecture

docs.title: The Best Part?
docs.text: Both use the same code! When you add a new feature, it automatically works in both the CLI and the API. Choose the interface that fits your use case, and switch anytime without learning something completely new.

docs.title: Next Steps
docs.text:
• Learn more about the CLI: Basic Commands Guide
  • Explore the API: HTTP API Guide
  • See examples: Advanced Usage

Still not sure which to use? Start with the CLI - it's easier to learn and perfect for exploration. Once you know what you need, switch to the API for production automation!

docs.title: Control Mode
docs.text: Master keyboard-only navigation with Inspekt Control Mode. Navigate pages entirely from your terminal using Tab, Enter, and Arrow keys.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
inspekt control provides keyboard-only navigation for accessibility testing and hands-free browsing. It's perfect for:

  • Accessibility testing - Verify keyboard navigation
  • Hands-free browsing - Navigate without a mouse
  • Screen reader compatibility - Test with keyboard + voice
  • Focus management testing - Verify focus indicators
  • Navigation persistence - Auto-refocus after page loads

docs.title: Starting Control Mode
docs.text:
inspekt control

What happens:

  1. Terminal enters raw mode (captures all keyboard input)
  2. Browser receives keyboard events in real-time
  3. Focus indicators appear on interactive elements
  4. Terminal displays announcements and feedback
  5. Mode persists across page navigations

To exit: Press Ctrl+D or q

docs.title: Basic Controls
docs.text: Key Action Tab Navigate forward through focusable elements Shift+Tab Navigate backward Enter Activate focused element (click/submit) Space Activate focused element Arrow Keys Navigate directionally Escape Return focus to body q Quit control mode Ctrl+D Quit control mode

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
Control mode captures your keystrokes and sends them to the browser:

  1. You press Tab in terminal
  2. Zen sends Tab to browser
  3. Browser shifts focus to next element
  4. Element is highlighted with blue outline
  5. Terminal announces element name and role

docs.title: Visual Feedback
docs.text: Focused elements get a blue outline (outline: 2px solid blue) so you can see what's focused.

docs.title: Terminal Announcements
docs.text:
Control mode announces element details in your terminal:

Focus: Submit Button (button)
Focus: Email Input (input)
Focus: Privacy Policy (link)

docs.title: Auto-refocus After Navigation
docs.text:
Control mode persists across page navigations:

inspekt control
# Tab to a link
# Press Enter → Page loads
# → Focus automatically returns to the link
# Continue tabbing from there

This is unique to Inspekt - the focus persists even after navigation!

docs.title: Text-to-Speech (macOS)
docs.text:
Enable voice announcements:

# Set in config.json
{
  "control": {
    "speak-all": true
  }
}

Focused elements are announced via macOS say command:

"Submit Button"
"Email Input"
"Privacy Policy Link"

Perfect for testing screen reader workflows without actual screen reader.

docs.title: Accessibility Names
docs.text:
Control mode extracts accessible names for elements:

  • aria-label attribute
  • aria-labelledby reference
  • Associated <label> text
  • Button/link text content
  • alt text for images
  • title attribute

This matches what screen readers announce!

docs.title: Configuration
docs.text:
Edit config.json in project root:

{
  "control": {
    "verbose": true,
    "speak-all": true,
    "verbose-logging": false
  }
}

Options:

  • verbose (default: true) - Show terminal announcements
  • speak-all (default: true) - Enable text-to-speech on macOS
  • verbose-logging (default: false) - Detailed debug output

docs.title: Example 1: Form Navigation
docs.text:
inspekt control

# Tab to first field → "Email Input"
# Type: test@example.com
# Tab to next field → "Password Input"
# Type: password123
# Tab to submit → "Submit Button"
# Press Enter → Form submits
# → Focus returns to submit button after page loads

docs.title: Example 2: Link Navigation
docs.text:
inspekt control

# Tab through navigation → "Home", "About", "Contact"
# Tab to main content link → "Read More"
# Press Enter → Article opens
# → Focus returns to "Read More" link position
# Continue navigating from there

docs.title: Example 3: Modal Interaction
docs.text:
inspekt control

# Tab to button → "Open Modal"
# Press Enter → Modal opens
# Tab through modal → "Close Button", "Save Button"
# Press Enter on "Close" → Modal closes
# Continue navigating

docs.title: Example 4: Accessibility Audit
docs.text:
inspekt control

# Tab through entire page
# Verify:
# - All interactive elements reachable?
# - Focus indicators visible?
# - Logical tab order?
# - No focus traps?
# - Keyboard shortcuts work?

docs.title: Combine with Other Commands
docs.text:
Take screenshots of focused elements: 

# Start control mode in one terminal
inspekt control

# In another terminal:
inspekt eval "document.activeElement"
inspekt screenshot --selector "$0" --output focused.png

Extract focused element info: 

# While in control mode (other terminal):
inspekt eval "
  const el = document.activeElement;
  return {
    tag: el.tagName,
    text: el.textContent,
    role: el.getAttribute('role'),
    label: el.getAttribute('aria-label')
  };
" --format json

Verify focus order: 

# While in control mode (other terminal):
inspekt eval "
  const focusable = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll(
    'a, button, input, select, textarea, [tabindex]:not([tabindex=\"-1\"])'
  ));
  return focusable.map((el, i) => ({
    index: i,
    tag: el.tagName,
    text: el.textContent?.substring(0, 30),
    tabIndex: el.tabIndex
  }));
" --format json

docs.title: Test Focus Traps
docs.text:
inspekt control

# Navigate into component
# Try to Tab out
# If trapped → Accessibility issue!

docs.title: Test Skip Links
docs.text:
inspekt control

# First Tab should focus skip link
# Press Enter
# Verify focus jumps to main content

docs.title: Test Keyboard Shortcuts
docs.text:
inspekt control

# Try:
# - Ctrl+F for search
# - Escape to close modals
# - Arrow keys for sliders
# - Space for checkboxes

docs.title: 1. Accessibility Testing
docs.text:
Verify keyboard navigation compliance:

  • All interactive elements reachable via Tab
  • Logical tab order (left-to-right, top-to-bottom)
  • Focus indicators visible
  • No keyboard traps
  • Skip links present and functional
  • Modals trap focus appropriately
  • Dropdowns navigable with arrows
  • Forms completable without mouse

docs.title: 2. Screen Reader Testing
docs.text:
Test with keyboard + voice:

# Enable text-to-speech
# Edit config.json: "speak-all": true

inspekt control
# Navigate and listen to announcements
# Verify meaningful names
# Check announcement order

docs.title: 3. Focus Management Testing
docs.text:
Test focus behavior:

inspekt control
# Open modal → Focus should enter modal
# Close modal → Focus should return to trigger
# Submit form → Focus should go to success message
# Navigate → Focus should persist (unique to Inspekt!)

docs.title: 4. Keyboard-Only Workflows
docs.text:
Browse without a mouse:

inspekt control
# Navigate entirely from terminal
# Perfect for accessibility demos
# Great for focus management testing

docs.title: 1. Terminal Setup
docs.text:
import sys, tty, termios

# Save terminal settings
old_settings = termios.tcgetattr(sys.stdin)

# Enter raw mode (no buffering, no echo)
tty.setraw(sys.stdin)

docs.title: 2. Key Capture Loop
docs.text:
while True:
    char = sys.stdin.read(1)  # Read single character

    # Handle special keys
    if char == '\t':  # Tab
        send_key_to_browser('Tab')
    elif char == '\r':  # Enter
        send_key_to_browser('Enter')
    # ... etc

docs.title: 3. Browser Script
docs.text:
// control.js (injected in browser)
document.addEventListener('inspektControl', (event) => {
  const {key, shiftKey, ctrlKey, altKey} = event.detail;

  // Simulate keyboard event
  const keyEvent = new KeyboardEvent('keydown', {
    key, shiftKey, ctrlKey, altKey,
    bubbles: true
  });

  document.activeElement.dispatchEvent(keyEvent);
});

docs.title: 4. Focus Tracking
docs.text:
document.addEventListener('focus', (event) => {
  const element = event.target;

  // Highlight focused element
  element.style.outline = '2px solid blue';

  // Send announcement to terminal
  const name = getAccessibleName(element);
  sendToTerminal(`Focus: ${name}`);
}, true);

docs.title: 5. Auto-refocus
docs.text:
// Store focused element before navigation
let lastFocused = null;

document.addEventListener('focus', (e) => {
  lastFocused = e.target;
}, true);

// Restore after page load
window.addEventListener('load', () => {
  if (lastFocused) {
    lastFocused.focus();
  }
});

docs.title: config.json
docs.text:
{
  "control": {
    "verbose": true,
    "speak-all": true,
    "verbose-logging": false
  }
}

docs.title: Verbose Mode
docs.text:
Enabled (default): 

Focus: Submit Button (button)
Focus: Email Input (input)
Activated: Submit Button

Disabled: 

(no terminal output)

docs.title: Text-to-Speech
docs.text:
Enabled (macOS only):

say "Submit Button"
say "Email Input"

Disabled (default on Linux): 

(no voice output)

docs.title: Keys Not Working
docs.text:
Problem: Keys pressed but nothing happens in browser

Solutions: 1. Verify browser tab is active 2. Check userscript is running 3. Refresh page 4. Restart control mode

docs.title: Focus Not Visible
docs.text:
Problem: Can't see what's focused

Solutions: 1. Check element has focus styles 2. Try forcing outline: 

inspekt eval "document.activeElement.style.outline = '3px solid red'"
3. Some elements have outline: none - accessibility issue!

docs.title: Control Mode Exits Immediately
docs.text:
Problem: Mode starts and exits right away

Solutions: 1. Don't press q or Ctrl+D immediately 2. Check terminal supports raw mode 3. Try inspekt control --help first

docs.title: Can't Exit Control Mode
docs.text:
Problem: Can't quit with q or Ctrl+D

Solutions: 1. Press Ctrl+C (force quit) 2. Close terminal window 3. Restart terminal

docs.title: Voice Not Working
docs.text:
Problem: No text-to-speech on macOS

Solutions: 1. Verify say command works: say "test" 2. Check config: "speak-all": true 3. macOS only - not available on Linux/Windows

docs.title: 1. Test on Real Content
docs.text:
Don't just test on example pages - test your actual site:

inspekt control
# Navigate your production site
# Verify real user workflows

docs.title: 2. Document Issues
docs.text:
Create accessibility audit reports:

# While in control mode, document issues:
# - Elements not reachable
# - Poor focus indicators
# - Illogical tab order
# - Keyboard traps

docs.title: 3. Compare with Screen Readers
docs.text:
Test with actual screen readers too:

  • NVDA (Windows)
  • JAWS (Windows)
  • VoiceOver (macOS)
  • Orca (Linux)

Inspekt control mode is a supplement, not a replacement.

docs.title: 4. Test Different Browsers

Keyboard behavior varies by browser:

# Test in Chrome
inspekt control

# Test in Firefox
inspekt control

# Test in Safari
inspekt control

docs.title: Data Extraction
docs.text: Master data extraction with Inspekt. Learn how to extract links, generate page outlines, get selected text, download files, and extract structured data from web pages.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Inspekt provides specialized commands for data extraction:

  • inspekt links - Extract and analyze links
  • inspekt outline - Display page heading structure
  • inspekt selected - Get selected text
  • inspekt download - Find and download files
  • inspekt info - Get page metadata
  • inspekt network - Inspect network requests

docs.title: Extracting Links
docs.text: The inspekt links command extracts all links from a page with powerful filtering options.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
inspekt links

Output: 

→ Home Page
  https://example.com/

↗ External Resource
  https://other-site.com/page

Total: 15 links (8 internal, 7 external)

Shows: - Link text (anchor text) - URL - Internal (→) vs External (↗) indicators - Summary count

docs.title: Filter to Internal Links
docs.text:
inspekt links --only-internal

Shows only links to the same domain.

docs.title: Filter to External Links
docs.text:
inspekt links --only-external

Shows only links to other domains.

docs.title: URLs Only
docs.text:
inspekt links --only-urls

Outputs just URLs (one per line), perfect for piping:

https://example.com/page1
https://example.com/page2
https://external.com/resource

docs.title: Alphabetical Sorting
docs.text:
inspekt links --alphabetically

Sorts links alphabetically by URL.

docs.title: Link Enrichment
docs.text:
Get detailed metadata for external links:

inspekt links --enrich-external

Fetches: - HTTP status code - MIME type (content-type) - File size - Page title - Language

Example output: 

↗ Documentation
  https://docs.example.com/
  Status: 200 OK | Type: text/html | Size: 42KB | Lang: en
  Title: Example Docs - Getting Started

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
inspekt links --json

Outputs structured JSON for scripting:

{
  "links": [
    {
      "text": "Home Page",
      "url": "https://example.com/",
      "internal": true
    },
    {
      "text": "External Resource",
      "url": "https://other-site.com/page",
      "internal": false,
      "status": 200,
      "contentType": "text/html",
      "size": 42170,
      "title": "Resource Title",
      "language": "en"
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "total": 15,
    "internal": 8,
    "external": 7
  }
}

docs.title: Combined Filters
docs.text:
# External URLs only, alphabetically sorted
inspekt links --only-external --only-urls --alphabetically

# Internal links as JSON
inspekt links --only-internal --json

# External links with enrichment
inspekt links --only-external --enrich-external

docs.title: Practical Uses
docs.text:
Export links for analysis: 

inspekt links --only-external --only-urls > external-links.txt

Count total links: 

inspekt links --only-urls | wc -l

Find PDF links: 

inspekt links --only-urls | grep "\.pdf$"

Check broken links: 

inspekt links --only-urls | xargs -I {} curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code} {}\n" {}

Extract and process with jq: 

inspekt links --json | jq '.links[] | select(.internal == false) | .url'

docs.title: Page Outline
docs.text: Display the heading hierarchy of a page for accessibility audits and SEO analysis.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
inspekt outline

Output: 

H1 Getting Started
   H2 Installation
      H3 Prerequisites
      H3 Setup
   H2 Configuration
      H3 Basic Settings
      H3 Advanced Options
         H4 Environment Variables

Total: 7 headings

docs.title: Features
docs.text:
• Native HTML headings - H1-H6 elements
  • ARIA headings - Elements with role="heading" and aria-level, marked with [ARIA]
  • Missing level detection - Gaps in heading hierarchy shown as [Missing] in red
  • Duplicate detection - Repeated heading text (2nd+ occurrence) marked with [Duplicate] in yellow
  • Hierarchical indentation - Visual tree structure
  • Colored output - Level labels in gray, text in white, indicators in color

docs.title: Accessibility Analysis
docs.text:
The outline command automatically detects common heading issues:

Example with issues: 

inspekt outline

Output: 

[Missing] H1
H2 Citrus Fruits
   H3 Oranges
   H3 Lemons
      H4 Varieties
         [Missing] H5
         H6 Growing Tips
H2 Tropical Fruits
   [ARIA] H3 Mangoes
      H4 Varieties [Duplicate]
   [ARIA] H3 Pineapples
H1 Stone Fruits
   [Missing] H2
   H3 Peaches

Total: 12 headings (4 ARIA) — 3 missing levels, 1 duplicate

Indicators:

Indicator Color Meaning [Missing] Red A heading level was skipped (e.g., H2 → H4) [Duplicate] Yellow Same heading text appears multiple times [ARIA] Gray Heading uses role="heading" instead of native H1-H6

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
inspekt outline --json

Returns structured data including issue flags:

{
  "headings": [
    {
      "level": 1,
      "text": "",
      "type": "missing",
      "is_missing": true,
      "is_duplicate": false
    },
    {
      "level": 2,
      "text": "Citrus Fruits",
      "type": "native",
      "is_missing": false,
      "is_duplicate": false
    },
    {
      "level": 3,
      "text": "Mangoes",
      "type": "aria",
      "is_missing": false,
      "is_duplicate": false
    }
  ],
  "summary": {
    "total": 12,
    "aria_count": 4,
    "missing_count": 3,
    "duplicate_count": 1
  }
}

docs.title: Use Cases
docs.text:
Accessibility audit: 

inspekt outline
# Check for:
# - Single H1 at the top
# - No missing levels (red [Missing] indicators)
# - No unintentional duplicates (yellow [Duplicate] indicators)
# - Proper use of native headings vs ARIA

Find issues with jq: 

# Count missing levels
inspekt outline --json | jq '.summary.missing_count'

# Find all duplicate headings
inspekt outline --json | jq '[.headings[] | select(.is_duplicate)] | length'

# List ARIA headings
inspekt outline --json | jq '.headings[] | select(.type == "aria") | .text'

SEO analysis: 

inspekt outline | grep "H1"
# Should find exactly one H1, and it shouldn't be [Missing]

Content structure: 

inspekt outline > page-structure.txt
# Document page organization with issue annotations

Compare pages: 

inspekt outline > page1.txt
# Navigate to another page
inspekt outline > page2.txt
diff page1.txt page2.txt

docs.title: Selection & Inspected Content
docs.text: Extract content from browser selections or inspected elements in multiple formats.

docs.title: Commands Overview
docs.text: Command Source Use Case inspekt selection Text selected in browser Copy highlighted content inspekt inspected Element from DevTools Extract specific DOM elements

docs.title: Quick Examples
docs.text:
# Get selected text
inspekt selection text

# Get selected HTML (formatted and clean)
inspekt selection html --compact --pretty

# Copy HTML to clipboard
inspekt selection html --copy

# Get inspected element's HTML
inspekt inspected html --compact

docs.title: Output Formats
docs.text:
Both commands support three output formats:

# Plain text
inspekt selection text

# HTML (with formatting options)
inspekt selection html --pretty --compact

# Markdown (converted from HTML)
inspekt selection markdown

docs.title: Compact Mode
docs.text:
The --compact flag creates documentation-friendly HTML by removing:

  • CSS classes and data-* attributes
  • Inline styles
  • SVG path data → [PATH DATA]
  • Base64 content → [DATA]
  • Long random strings → [STRING]
  • Empty comments
  • Long text (20+ words) → …

Example: 

inspekt selection html --compact --pretty

Before: 

<button class="btn btn-primary shadow-lg"
        data-analytics="cta-click"
        style="background: linear-gradient(...)">
  Click here
</button>

After: 

<button>Click here</button>

docs.title: Full Documentation
docs.text: For complete details on all options, see: Selection & Inspected Commands

docs.title: Legacy Command
docs.text:
The inspekt selected command still works but is deprecated:

# Deprecated - use 'inspekt selection text' instead
inspekt selected
inspekt selected --raw

docs.title: Download Files
docs.text: Find and download files interactively from the current page.

docs.title: Interactive Mode
docs.text:
inspekt download

Presents an interactive menu to select files:

Found 15 downloadable files:

IMAGES (8 files)
  1. hero-image.jpg (1920x1080)
  2. logo.png (400x200)
  ...

PDF DOCUMENTS (3 files)
  9. user-guide.pdf
  10. report.pdf
  ...

Select files to download (comma-separated, or 'all'):
>

docs.title: List Files Only
docs.text:
inspekt download --list

Shows available files without downloading.

docs.title: Custom Output Directory
docs.text:
inspekt download --output ~/Downloads/example-com

Downloads to a specific directory.

docs.title: Custom Timeout
docs.text:
inspekt download --timeout 60

For large files or slow connections (default: 30s).

docs.title: Supported File Types
docs.text:
Images: - jpg, jpeg, png, gif, svg, webp, bmp, ico

Documents: - pdf, docx, xlsx, pptx, txt, csv, md

Videos: - mp4, webm, avi, mov, mkv, flv

Audio: - mp3, wav, ogg, m4a, flac

Archives: - zip, rar, tar, gz, tar.gz, 7z, bz2

docs.title: How It Works
docs.text:
The download command:

  1. Searches for downloadable files:
  2. <img> elements
  3. <a> elements linking to files
  4. <video> and <audio> sources
  5. CSS background images

  6. Data URLs

  7. Categorizes files by type

  8. Presents interactive selection menu

  9. Downloads selected files in parallel

  10. Shows progress and file sizes

docs.title: Practical Uses
docs.text:
Download all images: 

inspekt download
# Select "Download all IMAGES"

Download PDFs from documentation: 

inspekt download --output ~/Documents/docs
# Select PDF files

Batch download resources: 

# Navigate to resource page
inspekt download --output ~/Downloads/resources

docs.title: Page Information
docs.text: Get comprehensive metadata about the current page.

docs.title: Basic Info
docs.text:
inspekt info

Output: 

URL:      https://example.com
Title:    Example Domain
Domain:   example.com
Protocol: https:
State:    complete
Size:     1280x720

docs.title: Extended Information
docs.text:
inspekt info --extended

Includes:

Language & Encoding: - Page language - Character set - Direction (LTR/RTL)

Meta Tags: - Description - Keywords - Viewport settings - Author

Resources: - Script count - Stylesheet count - Image count - Cookie count

Security: - HTTPS status - Mixed content warnings - Content Security Policy - Referrer policy - Robots meta tags

Accessibility: - Landmark count - Heading structure - Alt text issues - ARIA labels

SEO: - Canonical URL - Open Graph tags - Twitter Card tags - Structured data (JSON-LD) - Robots directives

Performance: - localStorage size - sessionStorage size - Service worker status

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
inspekt info --json

Structured JSON for parsing:

inspekt info --json | jq '.url'
inspekt info --json | jq '.title'
inspekt info --json | jq '.extended.seo.canonical'

docs.title: Advanced Extraction with eval
docs.text: For custom extraction needs, use inspekt eval:

docs.title: Extract Table Data
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  const table = document.querySelector('table');
  const headers = Array.from(table.querySelectorAll('th')).map(th => th.textContent.trim());
  const rows = Array.from(table.querySelectorAll('tbody tr')).map(tr =>
    Array.from(tr.cells).map(cell => cell.textContent.trim())
  );
  return {headers, rows};
" --format json > table.json

docs.title: Extract Product Data
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.product')).map(product => ({
    name: product.querySelector('.product-name').textContent.trim(),
    price: product.querySelector('.product-price').textContent.trim(),
    rating: product.querySelector('.rating')?.textContent,
    image: product.querySelector('img')?.src,
    available: !product.classList.contains('out-of-stock')
  }))
" --format json > products.json

docs.title: Extract Article Content
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  ({
    title: document.querySelector('h1')?.textContent,
    author: document.querySelector('.author')?.textContent,
    date: document.querySelector('time')?.getAttribute('datetime'),
    content: document.querySelector('article')?.textContent.trim(),
    tags: Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.tag')).map(t => t.textContent.trim())
  })
" --format json > article.json

docs.title: Extract All Images
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  Array.from(document.images).map(img => ({
    src: img.src,
    alt: img.alt,
    width: img.naturalWidth,
    height: img.naturalHeight,
    title: img.title,
    loading: img.loading
  }))
" --format json > images.json

docs.title: Extract Meta Tags
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  const meta = {};
  document.querySelectorAll('meta').forEach(tag => {
    const name = tag.name || tag.property;
    if (name) meta[name] = tag.content;
  });
  return meta;
" --format json > meta.json

docs.title: Extract Forms
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  Array.from(document.forms).map(form => ({
    action: form.action,
    method: form.method,
    id: form.id,
    fields: Array.from(form.elements)
      .filter(el => el.name)
      .map(el => ({
        name: el.name,
        type: el.type,
        required: el.required,
        placeholder: el.placeholder
      }))
  }))
" --format json > forms.json

docs.title: Extract Structured Data (JSON-LD)
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('script[type=\"application/ld+json\"]'))
    .map(script => JSON.parse(script.textContent))
" --format json > structured-data.json

docs.title: Text Normalization
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  const text = document.querySelector('.content').textContent;
  return text
    .trim()
    .replace(/\s+/g, ' ')      // Multiple spaces to single
    .replace(/\n+/g, '\n');     // Multiple newlines to single
" --format raw

docs.title: HTML Stripping
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  const html = document.querySelector('.content').innerHTML;
  const temp = document.createElement('div');
  temp.innerHTML = html;
  return temp.textContent.trim();
" --format raw

docs.title: Data Validation
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.item'))
    .map(item => ({
      title: item.querySelector('.title')?.textContent.trim(),
      link: item.querySelector('a')?.href
    }))
    .filter(item => item.title && item.link);  // Remove incomplete
" --format json

docs.title: URL Normalization
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  Array.from(document.links).map(a => {
    try {
      return new URL(a.href).href;  // Normalize URL
    } catch {
      return null;
    }
  }).filter(Boolean);
" --format json

docs.title: Scrape Multiple Pages
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Extract data from multiple pages

URLS=(
  "https://example.com/page1"
  "https://example.com/page2"
  "https://example.com/page3"
)

for url in "${URLS[@]}"; do
  echo "Extracting: $url"
  inspekt open "$url" --wait
  inspekt eval "({title: document.title, links: document.links.length})" --format json >> data.jsonl
done

docs.title: Export All Page Data
docs.text:
#!/bin/bash
# Complete page export

PAGE_URL=$(inspekt eval "location.href" --format raw)
PAGE_TITLE=$(inspekt eval "document.title" --format raw)

mkdir -p "export/${PAGE_TITLE}"

# Links
inspekt links --json > "export/${PAGE_TITLE}/links.json"

# Outline
inspekt outline > "export/${PAGE_TITLE}/outline.txt"

# Metadata
inspekt info --json > "export/${PAGE_TITLE}/info.json"

# Screenshots
inspekt screenshot --selector "body" --output "export/${PAGE_TITLE}/screenshot.png"

echo "Exported: ${PAGE_TITLE}"

docs.title: 1. Limit Results
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.item'))
    .slice(0, 100)  // First 100 only
    .map(item => item.textContent)
" --format json

docs.title: 2. Extract Only What You Need
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  // Good - extract only titles
  Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.item'))
    .map(item => item.querySelector('.title').textContent)
"

docs.title: 3. Use Efficient Selectors
docs.text:
# Good - specific selector
inspekt eval "document.querySelectorAll('.product .title')"

# Avoid - overly broad
inspekt eval "document.querySelectorAll('*').filter(...)"

docs.title: 4. Batch DOM Queries
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  const container = document.querySelector('.container');
  const items = container.querySelectorAll('.item');  // Query once
  return Array.from(items).map(item => ({
    title: item.querySelector('.title').textContent,
    link: item.querySelector('a').href
  }));
"

docs.text:

  • Advanced Usage - Complex patterns and scripting

docs.title: Network Requests
docs.text:
Inspekt provides two methods for inspecting network requests, each with different capabilities:

Feature inspekt network inspekt network har API Used Performance API DevTools Network API Requires DevTools No Yes (F12) HTTP Status Codes No Yes (200, 404, 500, etc.) Request Headers No Yes Response Headers No Yes Timing Breakdown Yes Yes (more detailed) Transfer Size Yes Yes Cache Status Yes (heuristic) Yes (accurate) Buffer Limit ~150-250 entries Unlimited Initiator Info No Yes

docs.title: Quick Start
docs.text:
# Basic network data (works always)
inspekt network

# Full data with status codes (requires DevTools open)
inspekt network har

docs.title: Method 1: Performance API (inspekt network)
docs.text: Works without DevTools. Great for quick performance analysis.

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
inspekt network

Output: 

Name                                  Type         Size       Time      Proto
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
main.js                               script       125.3 KB   245 ms    h2
styles.css                            stylesheet   45.2 KB    120 ms    h2
logo.png                              image        12.1 KB    89 ms     h2
api/data                              fetch        2.3 KB     340 ms    h2

Summary:
  Total requests: 42
  Total transfer: 1.2 MB
  Average time:   156 ms

  By type:
    script: 12
    stylesheet: 5
    image: 18
    fetch: 7

  Slowest: api/data (340 ms)
  Largest: hero.jpg (450.0 KB)

docs.title: Filter by Resource Type
docs.text:
inspekt network script      # JavaScript files
inspekt network stylesheet  # CSS files (or use 'css')
inspekt network fetch       # Fetch/XHR requests
inspekt network xhr         # XHR requests
inspekt network image       # Images
inspekt network font        # Fonts
inspekt network document    # HTML documents
inspekt network svg         # SVG files
inspekt network video       # Video files
inspekt network audio       # Audio files

docs.title: Sorting Options
docs.text:
inspekt network --sort=start  # Chronological order (default)
inspekt network --sort=time   # Slowest first
inspekt network --sort=size   # Largest first
inspekt network --sort=name   # Alphabetical
inspekt network --sort=type   # Grouped by type

docs.title: Show Domain Information
docs.text:
inspekt network --domain      # Add domain column
inspekt network --external    # Only third-party requests

docs.title: Limit Results
docs.text:
inspekt network -n 10                  # Top 10
inspekt network --sort=time -n 5       # 5 slowest
inspekt network --sort=size -n 5       # 5 largest

docs.title: JSON Output
docs.text:
inspekt network --json
inspekt network --json | jq '.summary.byType'

docs.title: Method 2: DevTools HAR (inspekt network har)
docs.text: Full network data with HTTP status codes. Requires DevTools to be open (F12).

docs.title: Why Use HAR Mode?
docs.text:
• See HTTP status codes (200, 404, 500, etc.)
  • Access request and response headers
  • Get accurate cache status
  • See initiator information (what triggered the request)
  • No buffer limit - captures all requests
  • Export raw HAR format for import into other tools

docs.title: Basic Usage
docs.text:
# Open DevTools first (F12), then:
inspekt network har

Output: 

HAR Data (DevTools)
Status codes and headers available!

Name                                  Status   Type         Size       Time
-----------------------------------------------------------------------------------
                                         200   document     15.2 KB    234 ms
main.js                                  200   script       125.3 KB   245 ms
styles.css                               200   stylesheet   45.2 KB    120 ms
api/users                                200   fetch        2.3 KB     340 ms
missing-image.png                        404   image        -          89 ms
api/broken                               500   fetch        512 B      1.2 s

Summary:
  Total requests: 42
  Total transfer: 1.2 MB
  Average time:   156 ms

  By status:
    2xx (Success): 38
    4xx (Client Error): 3
    5xx (Server Error): 1

  Errors: 4
  Cached: 12

  By type:
    script: 12
    stylesheet: 5
    image: 18
    fetch: 7

  Slowest: api/broken (500) (1.2 s)
  Largest: hero.jpg (200) (450.0 KB)

docs.title: Filter by Status
docs.text:
inspekt network har --errors           # Only 4xx and 5xx responses

docs.title: Timing Breakdown

Both methods provide timing information:

Timing Description dns DNS lookup time tcp / connect TCP connection time ssl SSL/TLS handshake time ttfb / wait Time to first byte (server response time) download / receive Content download time total Total request duration

docs.title: Post-Action Options: --open vs --reveal
docs.text: Many Inspekt commands that create files support two post-action options:

docs.title: --open
docs.text:
Opens the created file in your default application for that file type: - Screenshot → Preview, Photos, or image viewer - HTML → Web browser - YAML → Text editor - Video → Media player

# Open screenshot in image viewer after saving
inspekt screenshot viewport -o preview.png --open

# Open saved page in browser after saving
inspekt save --open

# Open video after recording replay
inspekt replay login.yaml --video --open

Use case: When you want to immediately view or edit the content.

docs.title: --reveal
docs.text:
Opens your file explorer (Finder on macOS, Explorer on Windows) with the file selected: - macOS: Opens Finder with file highlighted - Windows: Opens Explorer with file highlighted - Linux: Opens the containing folder in default file manager

# Reveal screenshot in Finder after saving
inspekt screenshot viewport -o preview.png --reveal

# Reveal recording file in file explorer
inspekt record --reveal

# Reveal video in Finder
inspekt replay login.yaml --video --reveal

Use case: When you want to copy, rename, move, or organize the file.

docs.title: Inspekt VM Behavior
docs.text: When running inside the Inspekt VM (Docker container), both --open and --reveal will download the file to your host machine instead, since there's no desktop environment in the VM. The download is triggered automatically in the control panel terminal.

docs.title: Element Interaction
docs.text: Master element interaction in Inspekt. Learn how to click, inspect, highlight, wait for elements, send keyboard input, and take screenshots - all from your terminal.

docs.title: Overview
docs.text:
Inspekt provides specialized commands for interacting with page elements:

  • inspekt click - Click elements
  • inspekt double-click / inspekt right-click - Double-click and right-click
  • inspekt wait - Wait for elements to appear/disappear
  • inspekt send - Type text into elements
  • inspekt inspect / inspekt inspected - Inspect elements
  • inspekt highlight - Highlight elements visually
  • inspekt screenshot - Screenshot elements

docs.title: Basic Click
docs.text:
inspekt click "button#submit"

Clicks the first element matching the selector.

docs.title: Click Examples
docs.text:
# Click button by ID
inspekt click "#submit-btn"

# Click link by class
inspekt click ".nav-link"

# Click by complex selector
inspekt click "nav > ul > li:first-child > a"

# Click by attribute
inspekt click "[data-action='delete']"

# Click by text content (using eval)
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('button')).find(b => b.textContent.includes('Submit')).click()"

docs.title: Using Inspected Element
docs.text:
You can click the currently inspected element (from DevTools):

# In DevTools, select an element ($0)
# In browser console: inspektStore($0)

# Then click it
inspekt click
# or explicitly
inspekt click "$0"

docs.title: Double Click
docs.text:
Double-click elements for actions that require it:

inspekt double-click "div.editable"
inspekt double-click ".file-item"

docs.title: Right Click (Context Menu)
docs.text:
Trigger context menus:

inspekt right-click "a.download-link"
inspekt right-click ".file-item"

Click Types

  • inspekt click - Single left click
  • inspekt double-click - Double left click
  • inspekt right-click - Right click (context menu)

docs.title: Waiting for Elements
docs.text: The inspekt wait command waits for elements to appear, become visible, become hidden, or contain specific text.

docs.title: Wait for Element to Exist
docs.text:
# Wait up to 30 seconds (default)
inspekt wait "button#submit"

# Custom timeout
inspekt wait ".modal" --timeout 10

docs.title: Wait for Element to be Visible
docs.text:
inspekt wait ".modal-dialog" --visible

# With custom timeout
inspekt wait ".notification" --visible --timeout 15

docs.title: Wait for Element to be Hidden
docs.text:
inspekt wait ".loading-spinner" --hidden

# Wait for modal to close
inspekt wait ".modal-overlay" --hidden --timeout 20

docs.title: Wait for Specific Text
docs.text:
# Wait for element with specific text
inspekt wait "div.result" --text "Success"

# Wait for error message
inspekt wait ".message" --text "Error" --visible

docs.title: Wait Use Cases
docs.text:
Wait for page load: 

inspekt wait "main.content" --visible

Wait for AJAX content: 

inspekt wait ".dynamic-content" --visible --timeout 20

Wait for form validation: 

# Fill form
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('#email').value = 'test@example.com'"

# Submit
inspekt click "#submit-btn"

# Wait for success message
inspekt wait ".success-message" --visible

Wait for loading to finish: 

# Click action that shows spinner
inspekt click ".load-more"

# Wait for spinner to disappear
inspekt wait ".spinner" --hidden

Timeout Default

Default timeout is 30 seconds. Adjust with --timeout flag.

docs.title: Sending Keyboard Input
docs.text: The inspekt send command types text character by character, simulating keyboard input.

Types into the currently focused element.

docs.text:

inspekt send "test@example.com" --selector "input[type=email]"

# Type into search box
inspekt send "query text" --selector "input[name=search]"

# Type into textarea
inspekt send "Multi-line text here" --selector "textarea#message"

docs.text:
Login form:

inspekt send "password123" --selector "#password"
inspekt click "#login-btn"

Search form:

inspekt click "button#post-comment"

docs.title: Typing Speed
docs.text:
The send command types at a realistic speed (character by character). For instant value setting, use inspekt eval:

# Instant value (no events)
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('#email').value = 'test@example.com'"

# Typed input (fires input events)
inspekt send "test@example.com" --selector "#email"

Input Events

inspekt send fires proper keyboard events, which may trigger validation, autocomplete, and other event listeners.

docs.title: Inspect Element

You can also store the currently selected element in DevTools:

  1. Open DevTools (F12)
  2. Select an element (inspect tool or click in Elements panel)
  3. In console, run: inspektStore($0)
  4. Then use: inspekt inspected

Workflow

Use inspekt inspect to find elements programmatically, or use DevTools + inspektStore($0) for visual selection.

docs.title: Screenshots

docs.title: CSS Selectors Explained
docs.text: Inspekt uses standard CSS selectors. Here's a quick reference:

docs.title: Basic Selectors
docs.text: Selector Example Description Element div Select by tag name Class .button Select by class ID #submit Select by ID Attribute [type="text"] Select by attribute Universal * Select all elements

docs.title: Combinators
docs.text: Combinator Example Description Descendant div p All <p> inside <div> Child div > p Direct children only Adjacent sibling h1 + p <p> immediately after <h1> General sibling h1 ~ p All <p> siblings after <h1>

docs.text:
# Fill login form
inspekt send "user@example.com" --selector "#email"
inspekt send "password123" --selector "#password"
inspekt click "#remember-me"

# Wait for modal to appear

inspekt click "#next-btn"

docs.title: Conditional Clicking
docs.text:
# Click only if element exists
inspekt eval "
  const button = document.querySelector('#optional-btn');
  if (button) {
    button.click();
    return 'Clicked';
  }
  return 'Button not found';
"

docs.title: Click All Matching Elements
docs.text:
# Click all checkboxes
inspekt eval "
  document.querySelectorAll('input[type=checkbox]').forEach(cb => cb.click());
  return 'Clicked all checkboxes';
"

docs.title: Wait with Polling
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  async function waitForElement(selector, timeout = 30000) {
    const start = Date.now();
    while (Date.now() - start < timeout) {
      const element = document.querySelector(selector);
      if (element) return element;
      await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 100));
    }
    throw new Error('Timeout');
  }

  const element = await waitForElement('.dynamic-content');
  return element.textContent;
"

docs.title: Hover Simulation
docs.text:
inspekt eval "
  const element = document.querySelector('.menu-item');
  const event = new MouseEvent('mouseover', {
    bubbles: true,
    cancelable: true,
    view: window
  });
  element.dispatchEvent(event);
  return 'Hovered over element';
"

docs.title: Focus and Blur
docs.text:
# Focus element
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('#email').focus()"

# Blur element
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('#email').blur()"

# Type after focusing
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('#email').focus()"
inspekt send "test@example.com" --selector "#email"

docs.title: Element Not Found
docs.text:
Error: 

Error: Element not found: .missing-selector

Solutions: 1. Verify selector is correct 2. Wait for element to load: inspekt wait ".selector" --visible 3. Check if element is in iframe (not supported directly) 4. Use DevTools to test selector

docs.title: Click Not Working
docs.text:
Possible causes: - Element is not visible - Element is disabled - JavaScript event handler expecting different event - Element is covered by another element

Solutions: 

# Check if visible
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.btn')?.offsetParent !== null"

# Check if disabled
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.btn')?.disabled"

# Force click with JavaScript
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.btn').click()"

# Dispatch click event
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.btn').dispatchEvent(new MouseEvent('click', {bubbles: true}))"

docs.title: Element Changes After Action
docs.text:
Some elements are replaced after interaction (e.g., React re-renders). Re-select after action:

# Wrong - selector may be stale
inspekt click ".btn"
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.btn').textContent"

# Correct - re-select after action
inspekt click ".btn"
inspekt wait ".success-message" --visible
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.success-message').textContent"

docs.title: 1. Use Specific Selectors
docs.text:
# Good - specific
inspekt click "#submit-btn"
inspekt click "[data-testid='submit-button']"

# Avoid - too generic
inspekt click "button"
inspekt click ".btn"

docs.title: 2. Wait Before Interacting
docs.text:
# Good - wait for element
inspekt wait "#modal" --visible
inspekt click "#modal .confirm-btn"

# Risky - element may not exist yet
inspekt click "#modal .confirm-btn"

docs.title: 3. Handle Errors Gracefully
docs.text:
# Use optional chaining
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.maybe-missing')?.click() ?? 'Element not found'"

docs.title: 4. Verify Actions
docs.text:
# Click and verify
inspekt click "#submit-btn"
inspekt wait ".success-message" --visible --text "Saved"

docs.title: Download files from a page
docs.text:
# List all downloadable files
inspekt download --list

# Interactive download with gum choose
inspekt download

# Download to specific directory
inspekt download --output ~/Downloads

# Quick workflow: browse to a page with resources, then:
inspekt download  # Select images, PDFs, videos, etc. interactively

The download command finds: - All images (including background images from CSS) - PDF documents - Video and audio files - Documents (docx, xlsx, etc.) - Archives (zip, tar.gz, etc.)

Files are categorized and presented in an interactive menu where you can: - Download all files of a specific type (e.g., "Download all IMAGES") - Download individual files - See file sizes after download

    value: item.querySelector('.value').textContent,
    status: item.dataset.status

" --format json > dashboard_data.json

docs.title: Scraping workflow
docs.text:
# 1. Login manually in browser
# 2. Navigate to data page
# 3. Extract data
inspekt eval "
  Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.product')).map(p => ({
    name: p.querySelector('h2').textContent,
    price: p.querySelector('.price').textContent,
    rating: p.querySelector('.rating')?.textContent,

# 4. Process with jq

docs.title: Testing & Debugging
docs.text:
# Test a function
inspekt eval "myFunction('test input')" --format json

# Check for errors in console
inspekt eval "
  window.errors = [];
  window.addEventListener('error', e => errors.push(e.message));
  'Error monitoring started'

docs.title: JavaScript Execution
docs.text: Master JavaScript execution in Inspekt. Learn inline code execution, file execution, stdin piping, timeout handling, error handling, output formatting, and advanced patterns.

docs.title: Execution Methods
docs.text: Inspekt offers three ways to execute JavaScript code in your browser.

docs.title: 1. Inline Code Execution
docs.text:
Execute code directly from the command line:

inspekt eval "document.title"

Best for: - Quick one-liners - Testing expressions - Shell scripts with short code snippets

docs.title: 2. File Execution
docs.text:
Execute code from JavaScript files:

inspekt eval --file script.js
# or
inspekt exec script.js

Best for: - Complex scripts - Reusable code - Version-controlled automation

docs.title: 3. stdin Piping
docs.text:
Pipe code from stdin:

cat script.js | inspekt eval
echo "document.title" | inspekt eval

Best for: - Generated code - Dynamic scripts - Shell pipelines

docs.title: Simple Expressions
docs.text:
# Get page title
inspekt eval "document.title"

# Get URL
inspekt eval "window.location.href"

# Count elements
inspekt eval "document.querySelectorAll('a').length"

# Check if element exists
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('.modal') !== null"

docs.title: Complex Expressions
docs.text:
# Array operations
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.links).map(a => a.href)"

# Object literals (wrap in parentheses)
inspekt eval "({title: document.title, url: location.href})"

# Filter and map
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('img')).filter(img => img.alt).map(img => img.src)"

# Reduce
inspekt eval "Array.from(document.links).reduce((acc, link) => acc + link.textContent.length, 0)"

docs.title: Multi-line Code
docs.text:
Use newlines and proper JavaScript syntax:

inspekt eval "
  const products = document.querySelectorAll('.product');
  const data = Array.from(products).map(p => ({
    name: p.querySelector('.name').textContent,
    price: p.querySelector('.price').textContent
  }));
  return data;
"

Multi-line Tips

  • Separate statements with semicolons
  • Use return for the final value
  • Proper indentation makes code readable

docs.title: Handling Quotes
docs.text:
Shell quoting can be tricky. Here are the rules:

# Double quotes - escape inner double quotes
inspekt eval "document.querySelector(\"h1\").textContent"

# Single quotes in double quotes - no escaping needed
inspekt eval "document.querySelector('h1').textContent"

# Backticks for template literals - use single quotes outside
inspekt eval 'document.querySelector("h1").textContent = `Hello ${name}`'

# Heredoc for complex quoting
inspekt eval <<'EOF'
const selector = 'div[data-value="complex"]';
const element = document.querySelector(selector);
return element?.textContent;
EOF

docs.title: Basic File Execution
docs.text:
script.js: 

// Extract all links
const links = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('a'));
return links.map(link => ({
  text: link.textContent.trim(),

}));

Execute:

# or

docs.title: File with Modules
docs.text:
Modern JavaScript syntax is supported:

extract-data.js: 

// Extract product data with validation
const products = Array.from(document.querySelectorAll('.product'));

function extractProduct(element) {
  const name = element.querySelector('.product-name')?.textContent?.trim();
  const price = element.querySelector('.product-price')?.textContent?.trim();
  const image = element.querySelector('.product-image')?.src;

  // Validate required fields
  if (!name || !price) return null;

  return { name, price, image };
}

const data = products.map(extractProduct).filter(Boolean);

return {
  count: data.length,
  products: data,
  extracted: new Date().toISOString()
};

mkdir -p ~/inspekt-scripts

2. Write your script: 

// ~/inspekt-scripts/extract-prices.js

return prices.map(p => ({

docs.title: Default Timeout
docs.text:
Commands timeout after 10 seconds by default:

inspekt eval "document.title"  # 10 second timeout

docs.title: Custom Timeout
docs.text:
Adjust for slow operations:

# 30 second timeout
inspekt eval "await fetch('/api/data').then(r => r.json())" --timeout 30

# 5 second timeout (strict)
inspekt eval "document.title" --timeout 5

# 60 second timeout (very slow operations)
inspekt eval "await heavyComputation()" --timeout 60

docs.title: Timeout Examples
docs.text:
Long-running API call: 

inspekt eval "
  const response = await fetch('/api/large-dataset');
  const data = await response.json();
  return data.items.length;
" --timeout 30

Wait for lazy-loaded content: 

inspekt eval "
  // Scroll to load content
  for (let i = 0; i < 10; i++) {
    window.scrollTo(0, document.body.scrollHeight);
    await new Promise(resolve => setTimeout(resolve, 1000));
  }
  return document.querySelectorAll('.lazy-item').length;
" --timeout 30

docs.title: Timeout Errors
docs.text:
When a timeout occurs:

Error: Request timed out after 10 seconds

Solutions: 1. Increase timeout with --timeout 2. Optimize your JavaScript code 3. Break into smaller operations 4. Check for infinite loops

docs.title: JavaScript Errors
docs.text:

TypeError: Cannot read property 'click' of null

    return element.textContent;
  } catch (error) {

"

# Combined

docs.title: Validation

Validate before operating:

  const element = document.querySelector('.submit-btn');
  if (!element) {
    return { error: 'Button not found' };
  }
  element.click();
  return { success: true };
"

function extractProductData(selector) {
  const products = document.querySelectorAll(selector);
  return Array.from(products).map(product => ({
    name: product.querySelector('.name')?.textContent?.trim(),
    price: product.querySelector('.price')?.textContent?.trim(),
    available: !product.classList.contains('out-of-stock')
  })).filter(p => p.name && p.price);
}

return extractProductData('.product-item');
